articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka complains about the smell of marijuana during her U.S. Open match
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka, the two-time defending U.S. Open champion, complained to the chair umpire that the smell of marijuana was bothering her early in her third-round victory over Kamilla Rakhimova on Friday.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka finally found something that could stop her at the U.S. Open: the smell of marijuana. The two-time defending champion complained to the chair umpire that it was bothering her early in her third-round victory over Kamilla Rakhimova on Friday. Sabalenka said she had never smelled the odor so strong as she did while serving early in the match. “I don’t know if it was, like, coming from the crowd or was from the outside because the wind blows it into the stadium,” Sabalenka said. “I don’t know. I just hope they’re going to be a bit more aware of that stuff.” Sabalenka was serving in the third game of the match in Louis Armstrong Stadium. She tossed the ball but then let it fall to the court. She did the same thing on the next point, with something clearly bothering her. She then approached the chair to ask for help. “I was like, guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please, to not do it around the tennis courts,” Sabalenka said, when asked what she was thinking of the time. “It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.” Other players, such as Nick Kyrgios and Maria Sakkari, have complained in the past about the smell of marijuana during their matches. There is a park behind the grounds where the U.S. Open is played, which is often the expected source of the smell. No fans were found to be smoking and ejected from the tennis grounds. “While we can’t control what takes place off the grounds of the USTA Billie Jean King National Tennis Center, we continue to be vigilant as we maintain this facility as a smoke free environment,” U.S. Tennis Association spokesman Brendan McIntyre said in a statement. “This includes enforcement by our security and guest services teams when they are made aware of any individual that may be smoking, making them aware that although it may be legal in NY, that smoking is not permitted on parks property including the tennis center.” The top-seeded Sabalenka eventually was able to laugh off the topic during her news conference after the match, including the idea that fans just might be looking for ways to further enjoy her matches. “Maybe it’s too fast so they want to slow down a little bit, so who knows,” she said. “I don’t know the effect from it.”

articles.title: US Open says 2 influencers whose credentials were revoked were 'improperly submitted' as vendor staff
articles.summary: Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, who run 'The VIP List,' claimed that their credentials were withdrawn after they posted a video of the passes, but the tournam...
articles.body:
Amid the debate around influencers at the 2026 US Open, the tournament is pushing back on two influencers who say they lost access after posting their credentials in a video.

Meg Radice and Audrey Jongens, two influencers who run New York restaurant and lifestyle account "The VIP List," claimed on Thursday that their US Open credentials had been revoked just two hours after posting the video.

However, in a statement to The Athletic on Friday, US Open head Brendan McIntyre said that Radice and Jongens were incorrectly credentialed. (McIntyre is also the managing director of the U.S. Tennis Association (USTA) and the head of USA Tennis content and communications.)

"These individuals were not credentialed as media or content creators," McIntyre told The Athletic. "They were improperly submitted for credentials on a staff list provided by a food vendor."

In a video posted on their social media on Thursday, Radice and Jongens said that they are "diehard tennis fans" and called it their "dream" to be credentialed for the event. They even acknowledged the rash of stories about influencers at the tournament, but said that it did not apply to them.

"We were there to be respectful and follow the rules and have a good time," Jongens said.

"And it was taken away, just because we wanted to show how hot we looked in our credentials," Radice added.

The influencer issue has been widespread at this year's tournament, thanks in part to an increase in credentials being offered. 54 content creators were credentialed as media in 2025, but the number nearly doubled this year to around 100, per multiple reports.

Historically, the US Open has tended to be among the rowdier Grand Slams, with the tournament encouraging crowd noise in a stark contrast to the quiet stands at Wimbledon and Roland-Garros. However, things have appear to be worse this year: Naomi Osaka's first-round match had to be paused after multiple influencers filmed and did photoshoots during play, to the point that the chair umpire had to ask them to take a seat.

Multiple players have weighed in on the issue, including Osaka, who told reporters on Thursday that she wanted people to "respect the sport" even if they were new to it.

"I feel like it's common courtesy to read up on the sport. Especially the etiquette. I feel like it could be a good thing for people to make the sport of tennis popular to their specific audience, but I think it has to be managed a lot better, especially in the situation like in my first round match," Osaka said. "Overall, I think there's huge positives … You want people to continue to grow the sport. I just think it has to be in a way that everyone knows the rules and the etiquette."

Coco Gauff, who was also asked about the issue on Thursday, echoed Osaka about etiquette, though she said that she was "one of the more lenient" players about noise in the arena.

"I think it's great to have a different demographic to the sport. I have no problem with influencers. I've met some of them and follow some of them online," Gauff said. "It's not just for the players but for the viewing experience, for those around … I definitely think it's cool to have a new demographic and I definitely think it helps grow the sport. But like with anything, any venue you go to, like if you're being invited to a red carpet, you wouldn't show up in jeans.

Earlier this week, Daniil Medvedev told reporters that there is "a lot more upside than downside" to their presence.

"The more we try to raise awareness about tennis, the better it is. The more popular the sport is. For sure there is some downside," he said. "But in general the more the sport grows the better it is. I trust USTA with what they're doing."

articles.title: World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka says she might 'get high' herself if the smell of marijuana at the US Open doesn't stop drifting into the stadium
articles.summary: Tennis News: World No.1 Aryna Sabalenka humorously addresses the cannabis scent wafting through the US Open, impacting her match performance. Discover how she’s handling the situation while eyeing her next challenge.
articles.body: Aryna Sabalenka has joked that she might “get high” herself if the cannabis smell keeps drifting around the US Open after briefly stopping her third-round match to complain about it.The world No.1 was playing Kamilla Rakhimova in Louis Armstrong Stadium when she noticed the strong smell and approached chair umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore while leading 3-0 in the opening set.Sabalenka ultimately brushed off the interruption and produced one of her strongest performances of the tournament, beating Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4 to reach the fourth round without dropping a set.But the cannabis smell came up again in her post-match press conference, where Sabalenka revealed just how noticeable it had been.Sabalenka explains why she stopped the matchSabalenka initially believed the smell could have been coming from somewhere in the crowd.While leading 3-0, she called over Asderaki-Moore and told the umpire: “Someone is smoking weed, do you mind … because it’s so strong.”Officials briefly searched the crowd, although they were unable to identify the source.Speaking afterwards, Sabalenka said she had no issue with people enjoying themselves away from the competition.“I was like, guys you can do whatever. You can smoke, whatever. You can relax as much as you can. But please don’t do it around the tennis courts,” she said.“It’s a bit tricky to handle that smell while you’re trying to compete at your best.”The Belarusian was then asked how “high” she was compared with the other Grand Slam tournaments, prompting a laugh and a joke that suggested the smell had already become difficult to escape.“High? The level?” Sabalenka said. “Now I can only hear weed stuff. If they’re gonna keep smoking I might get high.”Sabalenka was also asked whether it was the first time she had encountered such a strong smell while playing in New York.“That strong? Yeah,” she replied.She suggested the wind may have played a part, leaving her uncertain about exactly where the smell had come from.“Also because it was a bit windy. I don’t know if it was coming from the crowd or the outside because wind blows it into the stadium,” Sabalenka said.“I just hope they’re gonna be a bit more aware of that stuff.”Cannabis is legal in New York, and the smell has become a familiar talking point around the US Open in recent years. However, smoking is prohibited inside the tournament grounds.British player Katie Boulter had also spoken about smelling cannabis around the outer courts earlier in the tournament, saying she had experienced it while playing on Court 17.Sabalenka finds her rhythm as Townsend awaitsThe interruption did little to derail Sabalenka's progress.The two-time defending US Open champion faced a challenging test from Rakhimova but eventually came through in straight sets, backed by a superb serving display.She hit 10 aces, faced zero break points and moved into the round of 16 without dropping a set.That is significant given the form Sabalenka brought into New York. The world No.1 had not reached another final since winning Indian Wells and Miami back-to-back in March, leaving her searching for consistency as she attempted to defend her title.She is also fighting to retain the No.1 ranking. Sabalenka has held the top spot for 97 weeks, but will lose it unless she wins her third consecutive US Open title and world No.2 Elena Rybakina loses before the semi-finals.Her next opponent will be home favourite Taylor Townsend, who reached the fourth round for a second consecutive year.Townsend followed up her run to the last 16 at last year's US Open by producing another impressive tournament in New York, defeating 15th seed Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-7 (3), 6-3.That means Sabalenka now has a considerably tougher test ahead, but after arriving at the US Open short of her best form, she is beginning to find some rhythm.And if the tennis continues to improve, perhaps the only thing Sabalenka will need to worry about in her next match is the opponent — rather than what is drifting in from somewhere around the stadium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: US Open: Serena and Venus Williams fall in first-round thriller vs. Maya Joint and Hao-ching Chan
articles.summary: The Williams sisters are a combined 4-24 in singles and doubles in 2026.
articles.body:
The Williams sisters will be a one-off show at the US Open this year. That doesn't mean it wasn't a fun time for a crowd that hadn't seen Venus and Serena team up in four years.

The 14-time Grand Slam doubles champions lost their first-round match in the women's doubles event on Friday, falling 6-3, 6-7, 7-6 in a three-hour thriller to the No. 14 seeded pair of Maya Joint and Hao-ching Chan.

With Serena not participating in the singles draw and Venus losing in the first round to Sofia Kenin , they have no more matches to play at Flushing Meadows. Serena also participated in the mixed doubles event last week, winning and losing a match alongside Carlos Alcaraz .

Joint and Chan will face Nicole Fossa Huergo and Tamara Korpatsch in the second round.

Obviously, the Williams sisters didn't display the form that won them two doubles titles at the US Open in 1999 and 2009, not with Venus at 46 years old and Serena at 44 and playing competitive tennis for only the past three months. That didn't mean they didn't have their moments. They built momentum as the match progressed and held a 5-0 lead in the decisive tiebreak, only for Joint and Chan to charge back in the face of a crowd heavily against them.

It was the kind of atmosphere we haven't seen in a Grand Slam doubles match in years. The 20-year-old Joint, who also beat Serena in the lone singles match of her comeback, appreciated the opportunity.

"[Serena's] an idol of mine, both of them. I looked up to them growing up," Joint said in her post-match interview . "Just to be able to play them twice is amazing."

Serena struggled early, rarely landing her first serve and operating a step behind the pace of competition. She was broken on both of her service games in the first set, giving the seeded pair the early advantage.

The match got more competitive in the second set, with the teams remaining on serve all the way to the tiebreak, when the Williams sisters finally found the momentum they needed.

The two teams traded breaks in a thrilling third set, all the way up to Joint and Chan's comeback in the tiebreak. Venus in particular looked like the best player at the court for the final two sets.

Venus and Serena reportedly declined to speak with reporters after the match.

With the loss, the Williams sisters are now a combined 4-24 in singles and doubles action in 2026, numbers that don't count the US Open mixed doubles event and its significantly different rules. Joint is responsible for two of those losses, having beat Serena in the lone singles match of her much-talked about comeback.

The sisters lost their only other doubles match together, falling 2-6, 6-1, 10-8 to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns in the first round of Cincinnati last month.

Both sisters still playing is a testament to their love of tennis and competition, but the sport hasn't loved them back recently. Venus has lost 15 straight matches since opening her comeback last year with a win over Stearns, while Serena's return has been a start-and-stop affair due to a knee issue sustained in her singles match against Joint. Both are dependent on receiving wild-cards from tournaments looking for a draw, which isn't going to change anytime soon based on the reception they're still getting.

It remains to be seen where either player goes from here, with neither having anything to prove after their legendary careers. Serena has at least said she intends to play singles again, with the tournament TBD.

Even in a loss, however, they showed they can still produce the kind of moments their fans are looking for.

articles.title: Serena and Venus Williams lose in a match tiebreaker in their return to the US Open
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams are out of the US Open women’s doubles after losing in a match tiebreaker.
articles.body: Serena and Venus Williams were once again the main attraction at the US Open. Carlos Alcaraz sure wasn’t going to miss it. “I think there is no better plan (than) to watch the doubles, the Williamses once again, while getting a treatment,” the defending men’s champion said after winning his match. “I’m going to be ready for that.” The match was a thriller, with the sisters battling back to force a 10-point match tiebreaker, but then blowing a 5-0 lead and losing 6-3, 6-7 (6), 7-6 (10-7) on Friday night to Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint. It was the first U.S. Open match since 2022 at the Grand Slam tournament the sisters won twice. They battled back from 4-1 down in the third set to tie it, but then faltered late. Serena came back to tennis this year at 44. Venus has continued to play on tour at 46. Perhaps it was their ages, could have been Serena’s long layoff, or maybe it was nerves. But both double-faulted during the tiebreaker after they had played so brilliantly late in the third set and then in the first few points. The US Tennis Association said the sisters would not be available for comment. Serena ended up losing to Joint for the second time this summer. She fell to the Australian in three sets at Wimbledon in her return to singles play, and she and Venus then had to pull out of their doubles match after Serena hurt her knee. That delayed their return to the Grand Slam stage until New York, where they won in 1999 and 2009 and are now 27-8 in their 10 appearances. The match got a spot in the night session in Arthur Ashe Stadium — practically unheard of for first-round doubles. The sisters were once dominant in women’s doubles, teaming to win 14 Grand Slam titles along with Olympic gold medals in 2000, 2008 and 2012. They shared the No. 1 ranking in women’s doubles for eight weeks. It appeared a first-round loss in 2022 was their last time together, with Serena stepping away from tennis that year after winning 23 Grand Slam singles titles. She came back this summer and now has two heartbreaking defeats with her older sister. They also lost in a match tiebreaker at the Cincinnati Open. Venus Williams also lost in the first round of singles. Alcaraz won easily but two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka was finally challenged — by her opponent and by the smell of marijuana — in her victory. Sabalanka beat Kamilla Rakhimova 6-3, 6-4. The No. 1 seed was pushed in a second set that lasted 54 minutes — a minute longer than her entire previous match. Trying to become the first player to win three straight U.S. Open titles since Serena Williams from 2012-14, Sabalenka will face Taylor Townsend in the round of 16. Alcaraz returned to the round of 16 by beating Wu Yibing 6-3, 6-4, 6-1. Back for this tournament after missing four months because of a right wrist injury, the two-time champion will face No. 20 seed Tommy Paul, who edged No. 15 Alexander Bublik in five sets. “To be honest I’m better than I thought,” Alcaraz said.

articles.title: Serena & Venus Williams Top Stats, Highlights from Loss vs. Maya Joint, Hao-Ching Chan at US Open
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams weren't able defeat Maya Joint and Hao-Ching Chan despite a valiant effort at the 2026 US Open on Friday, suffering a 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7) loss in their first-round women's doubles match.
articles.body:
Serena and Venus Williams weren't able defeat Maya Joint and Hao-Ching Chan despite a valiant effort at the 2026 US Open on Friday, suffering a 3-6, 7-6(6), 6-7(7) loss in their first-round women's doubles match.

It marked the first US Open doubles match for the Williams sisters since 2022.

Chan and Joint gained the upper hand early, winning three of the first four games in the opening set.

While Serena and Venus responded with a break and appeared to start getting more comfortable as the match continued, they still weren't able to take the first set.

The sisters fared much better in the second set, holding serve in the first game before gaining a 5-4 edge. They were still unable to convert break point opportunities against Chan and Joint, resulting in a tiebreaker.

While Serena and Venus won the first two points and later held a 6-4 advantage in the tiebreaker, a long forehand from Venus and a double fault from Serena resulted in a 6-6 score.

Still, the sisters were able to force a pair of mistakes by Joint in order to stay alive and secure a third set.

Chan and Joint took control of the third set early, gaining a 4-1 lead that was highlighted by a long backhand from Serena on break point in the fourth game.

The Williams sisters quickly got back on track, winning three straight games and bringing the score to 4-4.

Both duos held serve over the next four games, setting up a 10-point tiebreaker for the match.

Serena and Venus jumped out to a 5-0 lead in the tiebreaker, although Chan and Joint won eight of the next nine points to move back in front.

A long forehand from Serena set up match point before Chan hit a winner at the net to seal the final result.

The Williams sisters struggled with self-inflicted issues during the match, as they finished with 26 unforced errors compared to 15 for Chan and Joint.

Still, it was an admirable performance from the 46-year-old Venus and the 44-year-old Serena.

The sisters have already established themselves as a legendary duo, winning 14 Grand Slam women's doubles titles together and boasting a perfect 14-0 record in Grand Slam doubles finals.

articles.title: Venus and Serena Williams' highly anticipated US Open return ends in heartbreaking loss
articles.summary: Venus and Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for a thrilling three-set US Open doubles match that kept fans on the edge of their seats.
articles.body: For the first time in four years, Venus and Serena Williams returned to the US Open court together Friday night in Queens. The legendary sisters were set to reunite earlier this summer at Wimbledon; however, Serena — who, at 44, is in the midst of a comeback after several years away from the sport — was forced to withdraw due to injury. Friday night, the two walked onto the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium to a massive ovation from the crowd. GROUP OF INFLUENCERS FORCES PAUSE DURING US OPEN MATCH WITH CRINGEWORTHY PHOTOSHOOT IN SUITE Serena's jacket listed her US Open titles, including the pair of doubles titles that she and Venus won in 1999 and 2009. Their opponents were Taiwan’s Chan Hao-ching and Australian Maya Joint, who, at 20 years old, was just a toddler when the Williams sisters won the 2009 US Open. The first set was fairly back and forth to start, but Chan and Joint pulled ahead to win it 6-3. The Williams sisters responded and started the second set strong, but it went the distance, needing a seven-point tie-breaker to decide the winner. In the tie-breaker, Venus and Serena had multiple opportunities to put Chan and Joint away, but they fought back. Finally, after the scare, the Williamses clinched the set to keep the match going. While they were respectful throughout the match, there was no question that the overwhelming majority of the crowd was behind the sisters, erupting after every point. articles.title: US Open: Serena and Venus Williams suffer agonising defeat to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching in a women's doubles first-round epic
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams suffer agonising defeat to Maya Joint and Chan Hao-Ching in a 10-point match tie-breaker at Flushing Meadows; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
In a fight to the finish, the Williams sisters rallied to force a third set tie-breaker in which they blew a 5-0 lead before falling to Joint and Chan 6-3 6-7 (8-6) 7-6 (10-7) in three hours and two minutes.

The legendary sister act were playing their first Grand Slam together since the 2022 US Open, and 27 years after they first won the title.

The comeback, which Serena said was at the suggestion ​of her daughter, carried the weight of more than two decades: 14 Grand Slam doubles titles together, two US Open crowns, three Olympic gold medals, and another 30 Grand Slam singles titles between ​them.

But it ended up being quite the summer for Joint, the 20-year-old Australian, who defeated Serena on Centre Court at Wimbledon in the women's singles before facing her in front of 23,000 adoring fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday night.

"Being able to play against such legends of the game is super special," said Joint on court.

"I'm lost for words to think of it," Joint continued. "She's my ​idol, both of them. I grew up in Michigan so I always looked up to ⁠them. Being able to play them twice is amazing."

It was certainly an occasion worthy of wild cards Serena, 44, and 46-year-old Venus were given as their every winner was cheered to the rafters of a packed stadium.

And there could be more to come from the 23-time Grand Slam champion after ESPN commentator Caroline Wozniacki revealed she believes Serena wants to return to singles next year.

They might have a combined age of 90 but the Williams' rolled back the years at times, and all of Ashe was on its feet when a penetrating Venus volley was put away by Serena's swinging winner.

But two breaks of Serena's serve - which had looked in good shape at Wimbledon and in her mixed doubles run-out with Carlos Alcaraz last week - cost them the first set.

They hit back in the second set tie-break, finally converting a fifth set point when a Joint overhead floated long.

The decider also rumbled into a tie-break, the the first time the duo had been past 5-5 in a third set since 2001.

But they stumbled badly in sight of the finishing line and a Chan volley ended the much-anticipated comeback.

The US Tennis Association said the sisters would not be available for comment following their defeat.

Greek star seals a career-first trip to the fourth round

Revitalised Stefanos Tsitsipas bounced back from a first-set loss to prevail over Czech 18th seed, Jiri Lehecka, with a 2-6 6-1 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 victory.

The Greek moved into the fourth round for ‌the first time in his career.

American 11th seed Frances Tiafoe eased past Valentin Vacherot from Monaco 6-4 6-2 6-4.

articles.title: US Open players can still be fined $50,000 for failing to fulfil little-known obligation even after defeat
articles.summary: Tennis News: Players at the US Open can incur a hefty $50,000 fine for not meeting post-match media requirements, even after their tournament run ends. Explore the obligations players must fulfill and the consequences of non-compliance.
articles.body: US Open players could be hit with a $50,000 fine if they fail to fulfil one of the tournament's lesser-known requirements, and the obligation can continue even after their hopes of winning the title are over.While the focus at Flushing Meadows is naturally on the matches and the record-breaking prize money on offer, players also have contractual responsibilities away from the court. One of those is attending the required media opportunities after each match.That means losing a match does not necessarily mean a player can simply pack their bags and leave.What happens if a US Open player refuses to speak to the media?According to page 49 of the Official Grand Slam Rulebook, players are required to attend post-match media opportunities at an appropriate and reasonable time following the conclusion of each match.Those obligations cover more than just the traditional press conference.The rule states that media opportunities include, but are not limited to, interviews with the host broadcaster and the player's national broadcaster. The singles champions also agree to participate in appropriate media activity when requested.A player who fails to comply can therefore face a $50,000 fine, unless they are unable to fulfil the obligation because of circumstances such as illness or injury.So, in practical terms, a player cannot simply lose a match and decide they would rather skip the questions before heading home. The media commitments remain part of their responsibilities throughout the tournament, including after elimination.There is already a recent example of how close a Grand Slam player can come to facing that punishment.At Wimbledon in July, Serena Williams chose not to attend her mandatory post-match press conference following her first-round defeat to Maya Short.Williams avoided a fine, however, after a quote attributed to her was released following the match. The All England Club determined that her decision not to attend was reasonable and that she had satisfied some of her media obligations by providing a response.At this year's US Open, no player had been fined for breaking the rule at the time of writing. But the potential punishment remains clear: $50,000 for failing to fulfil the required media duties, unless an accepted reason such as illness or injury applies.And it is not simply a US Open quirk. The issue has previously become one of the biggest talking points in tennis when a player decided they would rather not speak to the media at all.Naomi Osaka showed how serious the issue can becomeThe most famous example came in 2021, when Naomi Osaka withdrew from the French Open after refusing to participate in media duties.Osaka, who was world No.2 at the time, had announced before the tournament that she would not attend press conferences, explaining that she had experienced bouts of depression and social anxiety when engaging with the media.Grand Slam organisers subsequently warned that continued refusal to fulfil her media obligations could eventually lead to her being expelled from the tournament.Osaka ultimately chose to withdraw herself.In a lengthy statement, she explained that she believed leaving the tournament was the best decision for herself, the other players and the event.“This isn't a situation I ever imagined or intended when I posted a few days ago,” Osaka said.“I think now the best thing for the tournament, the other players and my wellbeing is that I withdraw so that everyone can get back to focusing on the tennis going on in Paris.”She also apologised for becoming a distraction and said she had struggled with depression since the 2018 US Open.“The truth is I have suffered long bouts of depression since the US Open in 2018 and I have had a really hard time coping with that,” she said.Osaka added that she was naturally introverted and that wearing headphones at tournaments helped with her social anxiety.French Tennis Federation president Gilles Moretton described her withdrawal as “unfortunate”, while also wishing her well and stressing that the Grand Slams, WTA, ATP and ITF remained committed to player wellbeing.The Osaka situation was ultimately about far more than a fine, but it demonstrated just how seriously Grand Slam organisers can take media obligations.At the US Open, the immediate consequence for a player who simply fails to fulfil the requirement is much easier to understand: $50,000 could be taken out of their pocket.And with the tournament's biggest stars still chasing the title at Flushing Meadows, articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz Explains Why He'll Take More Breaks During Tennis Season After Wrist Injury
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz revealed that he plans to take more breaks in 2027 after dealing with a wrist injury during the 2026 tennis season.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz revealed that he plans to take more breaks in 2027 after dealing with a wrist injury during the 2026 tennis season.

"I'm kind of a guy that doesn't need to play a lot of tournaments," Alcaraz said Friday, per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN ).

"I just feel like you can have those moments of time to have a break, to prepare well for tournaments, to prepare well mentally," he added.

The 23-year-old wrapped up a 6-3, 6-4, 6-1 victory over Wu Yibing in the third round of the US Open on Friday.

Alcaraz was previously sidelined for over four months due to a right wrist injury that he suffered at the Barcelona Open, causing him to miss Roland-Garros and Wimbledon.

He confirmed that he hasn't experienced any setbacks in his recovery during his current US Open run, though.

"It feels like I've been competing the whole time. So I surprise myself the way that I'm feeling and the way that I'm recovering after every match," Alcaraz said, via ESPN. "So I'm just really happy about it that I'm able to perform at my best after every match."

While a lighter schedule seems to be on the horizon for Alcaraz, he'll look to defend his 2025 US Open title and capture his eighth career Grand Slam championship for now.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Serena and Venus Williams prove they can still compete in Grand Slam doubles - but what does the future hold?
articles.summary: Serena and Venus Williams may have lost in their US Open doubles return, but the veteran pair proved they can still compete on an entertaining night in New York.
articles.body:
Rarely has a women's doubles first-round match headlined the US Open night session - but the Williams sisters are like no other pairing.

Serena and Venus Williams might have a combined age of 90, but their star remains undimmed. Neither does their ability to compete at the highest level when they are in tandem.

Even though the superstar siblings - aged 44 and 46 - lost on their highly-anticipated Grand Slam return, their performance in a narrow defeat by 14th seeds Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint led to an entertaining night in New York.

A packed Arthur Ashe Stadium roared on the American icons as they looked on course for a memorable win - but ultimately fell short in a 6-3 6-7 (6-8) 7-6 (10-7) loss.

"It was unbelievable how competitive that was," said former American player-turned-commentator Chanda Rubin, who lost to the Williams sisters in the 1999 US Open doubles final.

"After the first set you wondered if Serena and Venus would be able to find their mojo - but, boy, they did."

Four years after they last appeared on Ashe, the Williams sisters were given a rapturous reception as they strode onto a court where they have won eight singles titles between them and two doubles titles together.

The decibel levels were rarely matched in an underwhelming first set for the home favourites, but the noise quickly returned when they rallied in the second set.

The atmosphere became muted as the decider seemed to run away from them at 4-1 down, before they showed indomitable spirit - a hallmark of their extraordinary careers - to take their opponents into a first-to-10 match tie-break.

Racing into a 5-0 lead put the Williams sisters firmly on course to reach the second round, only for Chan and Joint to fight back - with the help of a double fault from each opponent.

Despite the initial despondency of the home fans, the volume was turned back up when the American pair were given a fond farewell - with everyone left wondering what the future holds for them both.

Serena hinted she wanted to play singles again in an interview with Good Morning America , external earlier this week, while Venus said after her singles exit on Monday that she should not "have to" think about her future beyond the doubles.

The questions about what happens next were not addressed by the pair following Friday's match. The sisters decided they were "not available" to speak to the media, US Open organisers said.

For once, the 20,000-odd fans on a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium sat quietly engrossed during points.

The sight of the Williams sisters back on court together at the US Open - possibly for the final time - commanded ultimate respect from a chatty crowd known to let their attention wander.

The siblings changed the face of the sport when they emerged as precocious teenagers in the 1990s, going on to dominate the sport with a combined 30 Grand Slam singles titles and 14 doubles victories as a pair.

Three decades later, the sport remains captivated by them.

Serena, a 23-time Grand Slam women's singles champion, coming out of retirement this summer sparked excitement among those who saw her in their prime and those too young to have witnessed it.

Seven-time major winner Venus has never "evolved away" from the sport - the words chosen by her younger sister when she last played in 2022 - but instead continued her career with the help of sporadic wildcards.

While that has proved controversial in some quarters, there were few objections about the sisters being invited to play once again at Flushing Meadows.

Their planned return at Wimbledon was scuppered by the knee injury which Serena suffered in her singles match there - ironically a defeat by 20-year-old Joint - before they finally reunited at the WTA event in Cincinnati.

The comeback ended in a match tie-break defeat by Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk and her American partner Peyton Stearns, with the same fate befalling them in New York.

When the Williams sisters last played on Ashe four years ago, they suffered a straight-set defeat by Czech pair Lucie Hradecka and Linda Noskova in the first round.

It looked like being a similar fate as they meekly surrendered the first set against Chan and Joint, then batted off four break points in the fifth and seventh games of the second set.

But once Serena upped her level to match her impressive sister, they managed to switch the momentum back in their favour and level the match.

An absorbing contest featuring some sensational points saw the Americans fight back again in the decider, only to falter from a commanding lead in the tie-break.

Overall it was a more than credible performance from the veteran pair. Their solid groundstrokes, sharp movement and never-say-die attitude caused problems for their opponents, who deserve huge credit for staying focused in a partisan environment.

"The atmosphere was surreal," said Joint.

"It was something we've never experienced before, and to play against such legends of the game was super special."

articles.standfirst: El tenista español cayó eliminado en la tercera ronda del US Open
articles.summary: El tenista español cayó eliminado en la tercera ronda del US Open
articles.body: El español Daniel Mérida quedó eliminado en la tercera ronda del Abierto de Estados Unidos, tras caer en tres sets ante el estadounidense Alex Michelsen. Michelsen (46 del mundo) se deshizo de Mérida (n.39) por 7-6(5), 6-4 y 6-3 en 2 horas y 9 minutos de partido. El estadounidense se enfrentará en cuarta ronda al argentino Tomás Martín Etcheverry (n.32) por un puesto en los cuartos de final. Mérida, de 21 años, llegó a la gira norteamericana sin haber ganado un solo partido sobre pista dura como profesional y la cierra con un balance de 8-3, tras alcanzar los cuartos de final en Montreal y la tercera ronda tanto en Cincinnati como en Nueva York. Su buen papel estas últimas semanas le ha permitido meterse por primera vez en el 'Top 40' del mundo. Este viernes, sin embargo, se vio claramente superado por su rival tras ganar solo el 60% de sus puntos al saque y el 28% al resto, ceder cuatro 'breaks' y convertir uno solo en sus cinco oportunidades de rotura. El rival de Michelsen en octavos de final del US Open será el argentino Tomás Martín Etcheverry, que derrotó a su compatriota Mariano Navone, el verdugo del serbio Novak Djokovic, por 6-4, 6-4 y 6-3 en 2 horas y 26 minutos. Es la primera vez que Etcheverry se mete en la cuarta ronda de un 'grande'. Además, se convirtió en el primer argentino en alcanzar esta ronda en Nueva York desde Diego Schwartzman en 2021. Francisco Cerúndolo tratará de seguir sus pasos este sábado en su partido de tercera ronda contra el estadounidense Taylor Fritz. Navone, por su parte, se despide de Nueva York tras protagonizar la gran sorpresa del torneo en la jornada inaugural, al eliminar a Djokovic, y después de imponerse al italiano Matteo Berrettini en segunda ronda. Por su parte, el griego Stefanos Tsitsipas se impuso al checo Jiri Lehecka por 2-6, 6-1, 7-6(3) y 6-1 en 2 horas y 33 minutos. En las rondas previas se había deshecho del francés Arthur Fils (n.11) en un exigente debut y del sudafricano Lloyd Harris (n.139). En la cuarta ronda, Tsitsipas se enfrentará al estadounidense Ben Shelton (n.9), que venció el canadiense Denis Shapovalov (n.48) por 7-6, 6-7, 6-3 y 6-4. Es la primera vez que Tsitsipas, que llegó a ser número 3 del mundo en 2021, alcanza una cuarta ronda de un 'grande' desde Australia en 2024. Tstsipas se había hundido en el ranking en los últimos meses hasta tocar fondo en el número 88, en junio de este año. El griego empezó a levantar cabeza en julio con su conquista del 250 de Gstaad.

articles.title: Venus y Serena Williams caen a la primera en su regreso al US Open
articles.standfirst: Pierden ante Hao-Ching Chan y Maya Joint en su primera aparición conjunta en Nueva York desde 2022
articles.summary: Pierden ante Hao-Ching Chan y Maya Joint en su primera aparición conjunta en Nueva York desde 2022
articles.body: La incombustible pasión del público neoyorquino marcó el regreso de las hermanas Serena y Venus Williams al cuadro de dobles del Abierto de Estados Unidos, donde las leyendas locales, de 44 y 46 años, transformaron la pista central en una auténtica caldera para medirse en un marcado choque generacional a las decimocuartas cabezas de serie: la taiwanesa Hao-Ching Chan, de 32 años, y la australiana Maya Joint, de 20, contra quienes perdieron 6-3, 6-7(6) y 7-6(7). A escasos minutos de comenzar el partido, el estadio Arthur Ashe parecía más un ring de boxeo que una pista de tenis, ya que el recinto se llenó de humo y de un espectáculo de luces. En el momento en que las hermanas Williams hicieron su entrada triunfal, la mitad de los asistentes sacó sus teléfonos para grabarlas y la otra mitad se puso a aplaudir. El espectáculo continuó cuando el encargado de lanzar la moneda antes del partido para determinar qué jugadoras sacaban primero fue el youtuber MrBeast, cuyo nombre real es Jimmy Donaldson y tiene 515 millones de seguidores en la plataforma. Pese a perder el primer set (6-3), el público neoyorquino ovacionó a las hermanas como auténticas leyendas. Durante el segundo set (6-7(6)), que se disputó con un largo y ajustado desempate, el Arthur Ashe rugió cada vez que la pareja estadounidense se acercaba un paso más a la victoria. Serena y Venus Williams, campeonas del dobles de los Abiertos de EE.UU. de 1999 y 2009, también fueron aplaudidas cada vez que se lucían en un saque. Desde las gradas se oyeron gritos como: "¡Vamos, hermanas Williams!", hasta tal punto que desde los altavoces del estadio repleto se pidió silencio durante el partido. En la última manga, que tuvo lugar en la tercera hora del partido, resonaron en el recinto muchos "¡oh!" a medida que Chan y Joint iban tomando ventaja. Y no fue hasta que el marcador se igualó a 5-5 cuando el estadio volvió a temblar por los gritos de alegría de la afición, algo que continuó hasta que el electrónico reflejó el 6-6. Durante el superdesempate del tercer set (7-6(7)), se podía mascar la tensión en el aire y, pese a que terminó con la derrota de las Williams, todo el estadio se levantó de sus asientos en señal de respeto cuando estas abandonaron la pista. Por su parte, las hermanas, que iban conjuntadas con unas zapatillas, falda y top de color blanco, celebraron sus victorias con un choque de puños y risas cómplices. El encuentro suponía una oportunidad de revancha personal para Serena. Tras cuatro años alejada de las pistas, la menor de las Williams cayó este verano en su regreso al cuadro individual de Wimbledon precisamente ante Joint. Las poseedoras de 14 títulos de Grand Slam como pareja volvieron finalmente a competir juntas el pasado mes de agosto en el torneo de Cincinnati, donde cayeron en su debut ante Marta Kostyuk y Peyton Stearns. Ambas jugadoras ya habían tenido actividad en la presente edición del Abierto de EE.UU. Venus fue eliminada el pasado domingo en la categoría individual por su compatriota Sofia Kenin. Por su parte, Serena ha acaparado los focos del Grand Slam neoyorquino tanto dentro como fuera de la pista. Fuera de ella, ha impulsado iniciativas comerciales con marcas como Heineken 0,0 y ha hablado abiertamente sobre el uso de medicamentos para perder peso con el fin de combatir el estigma social. Dentro de la cancha, la expectación fue máxima al formar pareja en dobles mixtos con el español Carlos Alcaraz. La inédita dupla superó su debut antes de caer eliminada la semana pasada en cuartos de final frente a Belinda Bencic y Flavio Cobolli.

articles.title: Sabalenka detiene su partido: "Alguien está fumando marihuana, es un olor muy fuerte"
articles.standfirst: La tenista bielorrusa habló luego en rueda de prensa de este momento durante su encuentro ante Rakhimova: "Pueden relajarse todo lo que quieran, pero que no lo hagan cerca de las canchas de tenis"
articles.summary: La tenista bielorrusa habló luego en rueda de prensa de este momento durante su encuentro ante Rakhimova: "Pueden relajarse todo lo que quieran, pero que no lo hagan cerca de las canchas de tenis"
articles.body: El olor a marihuana se ha convertido en un espectador más en la presente edición del US Open. Más allá de la pista 17, conocida por el fuerte olor a esta sustancia que allí se respira, el aroma llega también a otras canchas. Aryna Sabalenka dio fe de ello en su partido en el Louis Armstrong Stadium ante Kamilla Rakhimova. Sabalenka detuvo momentáneamente el partido por el olor que llegaba a la pista. Sonriendo, se acercó a la jueza de silla Eva Asderaki-Moore cuando ganaba 3-0 y le dijo: "Alguien está fumando marihuana, ¿le importa?... porque es un olor muy fuerte". Luego, en rueda de prensa fue preguntada por esta situación. "Le dije que estos chicos pueden hacer lo que quieran, pueden fumar lo que quieran, pueden relajarse todo lo que quieran, pero por favor, que no lo hagan cerca de las canchas de tenis. Es un poco difícil soportar ese olor cuando intentas competir al máximo nivel". Las quejas de Sabalenka se unen a las ya expresadas por otros tenistas en esta edición del US Open. Fue el caso del francés Adrian Mannarino que habló de lo que se vive en las gradas en algunos partidos con la presencia de influencers: "Huele a marihuana en la pista, se está convirtiendo en un zoológico. Son condiciones realmente inusuales. La gente entra como le da la gana, se mueve, habla... El torneo lo tolera, no sé si es lo mejor para los jugadores y para el deporte en general". Sabalenka incidió en que en su partido ante Rakhimova el olor era aún más insoportable: "Hacía algo de viento. No sé si venía del público o de fuera porque el viento lo llevaba hacia el estadio. Sólo espero que sean un poco más conscientes de estas cosas". Incluso tuvo un momento de hilaridad en la rueda de prensa cuando un periodista lanzó la siguiente pregunta: "¿Qué tan colocada estás aquí comparada con los otros Grand Slams?" A lo que Aryna contestó: “¿Colocada? ¿Mi nivel? Ahora solo puedo oír cosas de marihuana. Si van a seguir fumando, podría terminar colocada yo también”.

articles.title: US Open 2026: No British players left in the singles - but are there reasons to be positive?
articles.summary: There will be no British interest in the second week of another Grand Slam at the US Open - but is it all doom and gloom?
articles.body:
For the fourth time in five majors, there will be no British interest in the second week when the US Open moves into the latter stages.

Underwhelming performances at this year's Australian Open, French Open and Wimbledon led to a series of inquests into what was going wrong.

But there is not quite the same sense of doom and gloom, despite everyone being wiped out after the second round in New York.

"Do I think there could be an inquest? I always think there's things that British tennis could do better. So yes, definitely," said British women's number three Francesca Jones.

"Do I think it's something that's concerning? No, not at all.

"The level is getting better and everyone is dangerous on their day."

With the Grand Slam season now over for the singles players, BBC Sport analyses the positives and negatives in British tennis.

Another Slam semi-final and more top 100 players - the positives

Arthur Fery's extraordinary run to the Wimbledon semi-finals is the clear highlight.

The 24-year-old was ranked 114th in the world and needed a wildcard to play at the All England Club, but took full advantage to produce a performance which nobody could have predicted.

Fery was the only player to reach the second week at a Slam this year and has been heralded by British tennis bosses as proof their talent development pathway is working.

Nine Britons competing in the US Open main-draw singles - the most since 1981- is also highlighted as a sign of recent improvement.

That figure does not include 2021 US Open champion Emma Raducanu and Jack Draper, who both missed out with long-term injuries.

"We obviously want more and more competitors in the second week of Slams - just like the British public," said LTA chief executive Scott Lloyd.

"But the fact we've had four different British players make Grand Slam semi-finals since 2021 - you have to go back 30 years before Andy Murray to have four - shows there is no question that the direction of travel has improved.

"We've just got to keep driving for more - and that's what we're trying to do day in and day out."

Five British men are set to feature in the world top 100 after the US Open, with Fery, Cameron Norrie, Jan Choinski, Toby Samuel and Jacob Fearnley representing the highest tally since February 2024.

On the women's side, there will be two players - Katie Boulter and Raducanu - in the top 100, although Jones and Harriet Dart moved back to the cusp after reaching the Flushing Meadows second round.

"We've sent 12 players to the world's top 100 over the past eight years and four of those have played Grand Slam semi-finals," said LTA performance director Michael Bourne.

"I'm not sure what other period in the modern era where we've had that level of productivity. Hopefully the number in the top 100 will rise over the next year."

Injuries, trailing other nations and coaching issues - the negatives

Despite those figures, some will argue that Britain - with its rich tradition and spending power as a Grand Slam nation - is still punching well below its weight.

A glut of injuries for many British players over the past year has not helped the cause.

Former world number four Draper has barely played over the past year because of an arm injury, while Sonay Kartal - who cracked the top 50 last year - has also dropped outside of the top 100 following a long-term back issue.

Britain has fewer players inside the top 100 than the United States, Australia and France, who also benefit from the revenue generated by hosting Grand Slam tournaments.

It also trails nations such as Spain, Italy, the Czech Republic and Argentina, who are all heralded for their talent production.

But Britain cannot simply "pick up a plan" of what others are doing as every country has its own "tennis ecosystem", says Bourne.

Lloyd adds: "We're competing in one of the most internationally elite sports out there and the landscape is vastly different to 40 or 50 years ago in terms of the number of countries which have representation at the top.

"We're ambitious, we want to drive for more, but we honestly believe the indicators are positive. We're moving in the right direction and stronger than where we have been historically."

Encouraging more British children to pick up a racquet from an early age is crucial to developing the next generation of stars.

Draper, Raducanu and Fery - who entered the LTA system at a young age - provide the blueprint.

There are 4.3m juniors playing tennis annually with 1.9m playing every month, which Lloyd says are both all-time records.

But there is a concern that a lack of high-level coaching is stunting the development of many more promising talents.

Bourne admits the UK needs a "higher base" of coaches, adding that one of the LTA's key strategies is "spending time and effort" on developing them.

Chris Marshall, a senior performance coach with over 25 years' experience, fears many youngsters are being priced out of tennis because parents cannot afford quality coaching.

"To fund a 12-year-old at county level right now requires anywhere from £500 to £1,000 a month for coaching, travel, and tournament fees," Marshall, who founded the Young Champs programme to provide free and discounted coaching for children, told BBC Sport.

"It is a massive, stressful financial barrier that makes the sport a non-starter for the vast majority of British families.

"We can't sit around lamenting the lack of British interest in the second week when we are restricting the pipeline that feeds it."

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz: "Enseñé demasiado los pezones"
articles.standfirst: El tenista murciano bromea en rueda de prensa sobre la decisión de jugar con una camiseta interior
articles.summary: El tenista murciano bromea en rueda de prensa sobre la decisión de jugar con una camiseta interior
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz no rehuyó la pregunta que le lanzaron en la rueda de prensa posterior a su victoria ante Yibing Wu (6-3, 6-4 y 6-1) sobre su nueva indumentaria en el US Open. El tenista murciano apareció con una camiseta blanca debajo de la elástica sin mangas. "Creo que enseñé demasiado los pezones. Sentí que los podía esconder durante al menos un mes, un mes y medio... Ojalá no vuelvan a salir", afirmó Alcaraz con un gesto sonriente. Tras sus dos primeros partidos, su look había sido de lo más comentados al portar la camiseta sin mangas, que provocaba que se le viera el pezón tras algunos golpes. Eugenie Bouchard, ahora comentarista de televisión, había viralizado un comentario tras el primer partido del murciano con Roman Safiullin: "Love you Carlos but we’ve got to put the nip away (Te quiero Carlos, pero hay que tapar ese pezón)". Alcaraz dejó claro que la incorporación de la camiseta interior no había sido porque así se lo haya exigido su patrocinador. "No, fue decisión mía. Fue mi decisión. No me importaría tener que volver a jugar así, pero si podemos evitarlo, creo que es mejor", añadió.

articles.body: NEW YORK CITY: Aryna Sabalenka was distracted by the smell of cannabis wafting through Louis Armstrong Stadium midway through the opening set of her US Open third-round match against Kamilla Rakhimova. The world No. 1 turned to chair umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore to raise the issue.“Someone is smoking weed,” she said, glancing briefly towards her box before walking up to the umpire. “Do you mind? Because it’s so strong there.”Asderaki-Moore spoke to an official on her radio, making a smoking gesture before play resumed.Sabalenka sent down 10 aces in her 6-3, 6-4 win over the Uzbek.“You can do whatever, smoke whatever, but please, not do it around the tennis courts,” the 28-year-old Belarusian pleaded. “It's a bit tricky that smell while you're trying to compete at your best.”While Sabalenka is not the first player to complain about the smell of marijuana around Flushing Meadows, the sprawling tennis complex skirted by green spaces, this is the first time she has brought it up in a match.The Billie Jean King National Tennis Center is a smoke-free facility, prohibiting smoking, vaping and the use of electronic cigarettes inside the tournament grounds.“It was a bit windy today. I don't know if it was coming from the crowd or was from outside and the wind was blowing it into the stadium,” she said.Last year, Casper Ruud, the 2022 US Open finalist, spoke about it with Norwegian media.“For me, this is the worst thing about New York,” he said. “The smell is everywhere, even here on the courts. We have to accept it, but it’s not my favourite smell.”In the fourth round on Sunday, Sabalenka will face home hope Taylor Townsend, who knocked out 15th seed Diana Shnaider 6-2, 6-7 (3), 6-3.The Williams sisters, Venus, 46, and Serena, 44, playing their first US Open match since 2022 at the Grand Slam tournament they have won twice, lit up Arthur Ashe Stadium on Friday night, rallying from a set down against Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint in the first round of the women’s doubles.But just when they appeared to have seized control, shifting gears from 1-4 in the decider, the Williams let it slip. They blew a 5-0 lead in the match tiebreak, winning just two of the last 12 points, falling 6-3, 6-7 (6), 7-6 (10-7) in a shade over three-hours in the first night match.Alcaraz changes gearAs much as defending champion Carlos Alcaraz’s play has been dissected since his return from a four-month injury-enforced break, so too has his playing gear. The Spaniard, who, like his illustrious compatriot Rafael Nadal, has made the cut-off singlet something of a signature style, sparked a sartorial controversy this time with its generous armhole setting the internet abuzz.Alcaraz, who was kitted out in the ombre tank in his first two rounds, fading from chocolate to white, could do little as the fabric caught the wind as he breezed around the rectangle. He addressed the situation in his third-round match against China’s Yibing Wu, wearing a fitted white vest underneath his game shirt.The Spaniard powered to a 6-3, 6-4, 6-1 win to set up a fourth-round meeting with American Tommy Paul.“I think I saw my nipple too much lately. I felt like I could hide it for at least one match,” Alcaraz said in his post-match interaction, adding, “I feel really comfortable with another shirt (underneath). So I think I'm gonna stay like that.”Alcaraz noted that the vest was his decision and not that of his sponsor, Nike.“I wouldn't mind if I had to play again like that, but if we could do something about it, it was good. Maybe the second round was a little bit distracting for me, but not that much,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: US Open: No. 10 Amanda Anisimova and No. 22 Madison Keys suffer upset defeats in third-round play
articles.summary: Saturday's third-round play wasn't kind to women's top American seeds at the US Open.
articles.body:
Two top American women suffered upset defeats in the third round of the US Open on Saturday.

No. 10 seed Amanda Anisimova lost to No. 24 Anastasia Potapova in straight sets, 6-2, 7-5. Shortly thereafter, No. 22 Madison Keys fell to unseeded Zheng Qinwen, 1-6, 7-6, 7-5.

Keys loses final seven games in third set

Keys was eager to improve on losing in the first round to Renata Zarazúa at last year's US Open. She advanced to the Round of 32 with wins over Russia's Alina Korneeva and Hungary's Anna Bondár. But she ultimately fell short against Qinwen, squandering a 5-0 lead in the third set.

The defeat was stunning, considering how Keys played from the outset. In the first set, she dominated, winning 6-1 in just 23 minutes and losing only two points on her first serve. Zheng seemingly had no answer for Keys, beating herself by committing four double faults.

Zheng finally broke Keys in the second set, as the American wasn't as formidable with her serve. But Keys battled back as Zheng lost control on her serve. She was helped out on some errant forehand returns from Keys, however, and eventually won a tiebreak to force a third set.

Anisimova can't match last year's run to US Open final

Anisimova failed to follow up on last year's improbable run to the US Open final, defeating Iga Świątek and Naomi Osaka before losing to Aryna Sabalenka .

One of three American women among the tournament's top 10 seeds, Anisimova fell behind quickly, unable to hold serve against Potapova. She faced particular difficulty controlling her forehand, missing with several shots and letting her Austrian opponent take the advantage.

Anisimova also couldn't break Potapova's serve, losing her first seven break points in the first set. As a result, Potapova cruised to the lead while Anisimova constantly tried to catch up and could never quite get there. While she battled back in the second set, 46 unforced errors were too many to overcome.

The early-round exit continues a difficult year for Anisimova, who played in last year's Wimbledon final in addition to the US Open. She began 2026 at No. 3 in the WTA rankings.

But in the Australian Open quarterfinals, she lost to Jessica Pegula, who also defeated her at Dubai and Cincinnati. At Indian Wells, Anisimova fell to Victoria Mboko and later lost to Elina Svitolina at the Canadian Open.

In Grand Slam tournaments, Anisimova was defeated by Diane Parry at the French Open. And at Wimbledon this year, she fell to Madison Keys in the third round.

This story will be updated with more information.

articles.title: Trinity Rodman's US Open moment reveals an old habit in sports broadcasting: introducing women by their relationships first
articles.summary: Tennis News: Trinity Rodman, Olympic gold medalist and highest-paid women's footballer, faces overshadowing by ESPN's introduction as Ben Shelton's girlfriend at the US Open. Discover how Rodman's impressive achievements should take precedence over her relationship status.
articles.body: Trinity Rodman was sitting in Ben Shelton's player box at the US Open on Tuesday when the cameras found her.The ESPN commentary that followed introduced her as “Trinity Rodman, also known as Ben Shelton's girlfriend, and also known as a member of the US women's national team.” The on-screen graphic was similarly arranged: “Ben's girlfriend & USWNT player.”Rodman is, of course, Shelton's girlfriend. The two tennis and football stars made their relationship public in March 2025, after Rodman slid into Shelton's DMs. Shelton, 23, is one of American tennis's leading players, a left-handed power hitter who reached a career-high world No.5 in late 2025 and has already won four ATP titles in 2026, including the National Bank Open two weeks before the US Open.But Rodman has spent the better part of her career becoming recognisable without him.The 24-year-old is an Olympic gold medallist, an NWSL champion and the highest-paid women's footballer in the world. She is also the daughter of NBA Hall of Famer Dennis Rodman, another fact that has often followed her into introductions of her own.The ESPN description prompted a familiar reaction from fans online, particularly because there was no shortage of things from Rodman's own career that could have been used instead.“Geez… she is so much more than Ben's girlfriend,” one fan wrote.Another put it more bluntly: “Trin is an Olympic gold medalist, NWSL player and then Ben's girlfriend. In that order.”Rodman's career does not need Shelton's name attached to itRodman's football career began long before she became a fixture in Shelton's box.The Washington Spirit selected her No.2 overall in the 2021 NWSL Draft when she was 18, making her the youngest player ever selected at the time. She won the league's Rookie of the Year award and helped Washington win the NWSL Championship in her first season.Three years later, she produced one of the defining moments of her international career.In the 2024 Paris Olympics final, Rodman scored in extra time against Japan as the United States won women's football gold for the first time since 2012. She now has 13 goals in 57 appearances for the USWNT.At club level, her value has grown just as quickly. Rodman became the first player signed under the NWSL's High Impact Player rule and agreed a landmark deal with Washington worth more than $1 million per season through 2028, making her the highest-paid player in the league.There is also the question of her surname, which has brought its own assumptions.Rodman has spoken openly about her complicated relationship with her father and rejected the idea that the name defines her.“He’s not a dad. Maybe by blood, but nothing else,” she said on Call Her Daddy.“I love to have my last name and when I say Rodman, it’s not my dad’s name, it’s my name.”She has been less defensive about being known as Shelton's partner. In fact, Rodman has said she actually likes the term WAG, even while acknowledging why some people dislike it.“For me, I think I like the term personally because, like I said before, I feel like 24/7 I'm on in front of cameras, and so I think I use the term WAG for me to simplify what I'm doing,” she said on Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce in August.“For me, saying WAG, it's me being like, ‘I'm Ben's girlfriend.’ But I can understand why it's so hated.”She described being able to share that experience with Shelton as “the best feeling in the world”, pointing to the fact that both are constantly training, competing and exhausting themselves doing the sports they love.That distinction matters. Rodman choosing to embrace the label is not the same thing as it being the most useful way to introduce her.This has happened beforeThe US Open moment was not the first time Rodman's identity has been filtered through the people around her.At Wimbledon in 2025, she was introduced during one of Shelton's matches as “Tiffany” and had her father mentioned in the same breath.This time, the mistake was different. Her name was right, her relationship was real and her football career was acknowledged. Yet the order still said something: Ben's girlfriend first, USWNT player second.There was plenty of room for a different introduction.Rodman was not simply another celebrity sitting in a tennis player's box. She was an Olympic champion watching another elite American athlete compete at one of the biggest sporting events in the world.She can be Ben Shelton's girlfriend. She can be Dennis Rodman's daughter. She can even happily call herself a WAG.None of those things requires her own achievements to come second.At 24, Trinity Rodman has already built a career substantial enough to stand on its own. At the US Open, she happened to be there to support someone else.For once, she deserved the spotlight without needing to be introduced through him.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Despite success for Coco Gauff on Saturday, the American charge at the US Open faltered badly after defeats for Taylor Fritz, Madison Keys and Amanda Anisimova; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.

The 22-year-old will next face the winner of compatriot Iva Jovic vs the Philippines's Alexandra Eala for a quarter-final spot.

"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.

"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."

Yet, the American charge faltered badly at Flushing Meadows after stunning defeats for Fritz, Keys and Anisimova.

Fritz, the ninth seed, looked to be cruising into the fourth round when he moved two sets ahead of Argentina's Federico Cerundolo.

The 28-year-old, runner-up two years ago, had not dropped a set all week and appeared to be on the verge of joining compatriots Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe, Tommy Paul and Alex Michelson in the last 16.

But Cerundolo, the surprise winner at Queen's Club earlier this summer, scrapped his way back into an error-heavy match and won 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4.

The host nation is still looking for its first men's singles title winner since 2003, when Andy Roddick beat Juan Carlos Ferrero in the final.

Paul, the 20th seed, takes on Carlos Alcaraz in what should be a first genuine test of the defending champion's title credentials following his return from injury.

"I think I played Carlos more than anybody on tour, for me, which is kind of crazy," he said. "We've had some good matches.

"But, I mean, he's the test, him and (Jannik) Sinner. They have been playing great, and I guess Carlos we haven't really seen too much, but he's obviously doing pretty well coming right back to competition."

Elsewhere, Belgian 28th seed Alexander Blockx stunned Italian fifth seed Flavio Cobolli 6-7 (4-7) 6-3 ‌6-0 6-3 to advance to the fourth round, where he will meet Argentina's ​24th-seeded Cerundolo.

Zheng stuns to knock out Keys after latter led 5-0 in third set

Keys, the 2017 runner-up, was crestfallen after blowing a healthy lead to lose 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 to China's Qinwen Zheng.

The 31-year-old said: "I feel like I obviously got off to a really good lead, and then I just got really scared, like I couldn't swing.

"I don't know. Tennis just feels really hard right now, so I feel like that kind of took over."

Last year's beaten finalist Anisimova hit 46 unforced errors in a 6-2 7-5 defeat by Austrian Anastasia Potapova.

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva beat Czech Nikola ​Bartunkova 6-2 7-6 (7-5) to advance to the fourth round at the US Open for the first time. The Russian fifth seed next faces Potapova.

Six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek dug deep to defeat Czech 25th seed Marie Bouzkova 7-6 (7-3) 7-6 (7-3) and reach ‌the fourth round. The eighth-seeded Pole will next face Qinwen.

Meanwhile, Serena and Venus Williams escaped a fine for not talking to the media after their defeat in the doubles on Friday night.

The superstar sisters were beaten in three tight sets by Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching in their first match at Flushing Meadows in four years.

articles.title: US Open: No. 5 Flavio Cobolli falls to No. 28 Alexander Blockx, No. 9 Taylor Fritz upset by No. 24 Francisco Cerúndolo in third round
articles.summary: Cerúndolo upset a higher seed at the US Open after his younger brother Juan Manuel stunned Jannik Sinner at the French Open earlier this year.
articles.body:
In a disappointing day for higher seeds at the US Open on Saturday, No. 5 Flavio Cobolli lost decisively to No, 28 Alexander Blockx in four sets, 6-7, 6-3, 6-0, 6-3. And No. 9 Taylor Fritz lost the final three sets of his match with No. 24 Francisco Cerúndolo in a 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4 defeat.

Blockx and Cerúndolo will now face each other in the Round of 16 on Monday.

Earlier in the day, No. 10 women's seed Amanda Anisimova and No. 22 Madison Keys suffered third-round upset defeats .

Flavio Cobolli could not recover after first-set tiebreaker

Cobolli took an early lead over Blockx in the first set, going ahead 4-2. But the Belgian came back to force a tiebreak and that effort may have worn Cobolli out — or at the very least, shook his confidence, and he could never quite recover.

Taking the first set to a tiebreaker after falling behind appeared to lift Blockx's confidence, while Cobolli looked baffled that the match slipped out of his control so definitively.

For Cobolli, the result was stunning in light of him apparently taking a significant step in his progression after advancing to the French Open final, where he lost to Alexander Zverev in a grueling five-set battle. That performance vaulted the Italian star into the top 10 of the world rankings.

Yet he got off to slow starts in his previous two matches at the US Open. In his first-round match versus Francisco Comesaña, Cobolli lost the first two sets before rallying for a five-set victory. And in the second round, he went down in the first set to Tristan Schoolkate. The mental and physical hurdles presented by overcoming those early deficits may have caught up with him in the third round.

The defeat is the second consecutive upset loss in a Grand Slam tournament this season for Cobolli. At Wimbledon as the No. 9 seed, he lost to wild card (and British home crowd favorite) Arthur Fery in three sets

Blockx advances to the Round of 16 for the first time in a Grand Slam tournament. Cobolli fails to get past the third round for the second consecutive US Open after needing to retire against Lorenzo Musetti last year.

Taylor Fritz suffered surprising collapse after early lead

Fritz appeared to be on his way to a straight-set victory after winning the first two sets rather comfortably. He wasn't completely sharp in taking that early lead, but didn't need to be as Cerúndolo committed a handful of unforced errors on his end. Additionally, he showed little defense on Fritz's returns.

However, Cerúndolo didn't let Fritz pull away, forcing him to work hard to avoid breaks on several points. One sequence in that first set was particularly compelling, resulting in a 20-shot rally. But after Cerúndolo finally broke Fritz, the American countered to break back and won that first set.

In the second set, Fritz took control early with his serve and hit several forehands that Cerúndolo couldn't reach or return. Additionally, Cerúndolo struggled with his serve, which allowed Fritz to seize control and take a two-set lead.

Early on in the third set, Fritz had the momentum while Cerúndolo became frustrated and looked like he was going to suffer a straight-set defeat. But Cerúndolo broke Fritz to tie the game at 1-1, allowing him to find his footing and settle himself.

From there, Fritz began to fall apart, suddenly committing unforced errors that he avoided while winning the first two sets. After losing the third set, Fritz was still in position to win the match. However, his composure appeared to crumble as he continued making unforced errors. At one point, he showed frustration and looked to his coaches' box for answers that weren't coming.

By the fourth set, the match made a surprising 180-degree turn. Cerúndolo gained confidence with each game and took control, while Fritz looked overmatched and consistently lost his serve.

Since reaching the US Open final in 2024, where he lost to Jannik Sinner , Fritz lost to Novak Djokovic in the quarterfinals of last year's tournament and couldn't advance past the third round this year.

It's been a good year for the Cerúndolo brothers in Grand Slam tournaments. At the French Open earlier this year, Francisco's younger brother Juan Manuel upset Sinner, ranked as the World No. 1 , in the second round.

On Saturday, Taylor Fritz's quest for the US Open title ended stunningly in a thrilling five-set match, which he once led by two sets.

In the women's draw, Coco Gauff stayed in top form, while Madison Keys lost, despite leading 5-0 in the third set.

Everything you need, from top takeaways to tomorrow's schedule, is below.

No. 28 Alexander Blockx def. No. 5 Flavio Cobolli, 6-7 (4), 6-3, 6-0, 6-3

No. 24 Francisco Cerundolo def. No. 9 Taylor Fritz, 3-6, 4-6, 6-3, 6-4, 6-4

No. 21 Luciano Darderi def. Dane Sweeny, 6-4, 6-3, 6-3

Karen Khachanov def. Benjamin Bonzi, 6-3, 6-2, 6-4

Taylor Fritz's quest to reach the Round of 16 in New York for the fourth year in a row ended in stunning fashion.

The 2024 US Open finalist lost to Francisco Cerundolo in five sets, despite having a two-set lead.

Fritz started strong, aggressively attacking Cerundolo's second serve and taking advantage of the Argentinian's inconsistency.

However, Cerundolo rallied in the final three sets, unleashing his signature forehand.

Despite his impressive form entering the match, Fritz finished with 54 unforced errors and won only 67 percent of points on his first serve.

The Round of 16 at the US Open kicks off Sunday on ESPN, with all matches also being available on ESPN Unlimited.

Tomas Martin Etcheverry (27) vs. Alex Michelsen

Daniil Medvedev (7) vs. Frances Tiafoe (11)

Match of the Day: Carlos Alcaraz (2) vs. Tommy Paul (20)

On Sunday, Tommy Paul will look to reach the US Open quarterfinals for the first time in his career.

The 29-year-old has made the last eight at every other major, but not yet in New York.

This year's chance to achieve that milestone will be challenging, as Carlos Alcaraz stands on the opposite side of the net.

Alcaraz is aiming to become the first repeat US Open champion since Roger Federer.

The 23-year-old Spaniard came into the tournament after a four-month break to deal with a wrist injury.

You could see the rust in his earlier matches, especially in his third-round win over Yibing Wu.

Alcaraz racked up 33 unforced errors, struggling to find consistency on his dangerous forehand.

Although the seven-time major champion has a 6-2 record against Paul, his current form gives Paul a genuine opportunity to cause an upset.

That being said, Alcaraz should have just enough in store to advance.

articles.summary: International Sports News: Carlos Alcaraz has reached the top of tennis, but his journey was not always easy. His family had limited money for his early tennis career, meaning t.
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz has reached the top of tennis, but his journey was not always easy. His family had limited money for his early tennis career, meaning they needed outside help to send him to tournaments. Years later, after becoming a Grand Slam champion, Alcaraz faced a different struggle when a wrist injury kept him out for almost five months in 2026. Those moments tested him in very different ways.Carlos Alcaraz and his family’s financial struggle in his early tennis yearsAlcaraz grew up in a family where tennis was already important. His father, Carlos Alcaraz Sr., had also wanted to become a professional player, but he did not have enough money to take that dream further. He later worked as a tennis coach and administrator.When young Carlos began travelling for tournaments, his own family faced a similar problem. Tennis required money for coaching, travel and other costs, and the family could not pay for everything on its own.His early coach, Kiko Navarro, helped find support from Postres Reina, a local confectionery company in Murcia. According to The Guardian, the company helped pay for Alcaraz’s trips to tournaments after Navarro asked for financial support.That help mattered because Alcaraz was still only a young player trying to build his career. He had the talent, but he also needed the chance to compete and improve.The support continued as he began travelling around Spain and Europe. His family also had to accept another difficult change when Alcaraz moved away from home to train at Juan Carlos Ferrero’s Equelite Sport Academy in Villena.Navarro told The Guardian that the move was difficult for Alcaraz because he missed his friends and family in Murcia. He still returned home on weekends, but leaving the place where he had grown up was another part of growing into a professional player.Those sacrifices eventually opened the door to the career he has today.Carlos Alcaraz’s injury struggle and mental battle in 2026By 2026, Alcaraz was no longer a young player looking for an opportunity. He was a seven-time Grand Slam champion and had completed his career Grand Slam by winning the Australian Open.Then came another major test.A wrist injury suffered in April kept Alcaraz away from singles tennis for nearly five months. He missed the French Open, Wimbledon and other important tournaments. For someone used to spending much of the year competing, suddenly having to wait was difficult.The hardest part was not only the injury itself. Alcaraz told Reuters that the uncertainty around his return led to “intrusive thoughts” and was the most challenging part of his time away from the court.He finally returned to singles at the 2026 US Open, beating Roman Safiullin in straight sets. He then continued his title defence by defeating Wu Yibing and reaching the fourth round.The return showed how different his struggles had become. As a child, Alcaraz needed financial support to keep travelling for tournaments. Years later, he had everything a young player could dream of, yet an injury forced him to step away from the sport.His story is therefore not about having an unusually difficult childhood. It is about facing problems at different stages and continuing to move forward.
