articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Zheng Qinwen beats Madison Keys from match point down to reach fourth round
articles.summary: Zheng Qinwen fights back from 5-0 down in the deciding set and stares down match point to stun American 22nd seed Madison Keys.
articles.body:
Zheng Qinwen described her US Open third-round comeback win over Madison Keys as a "very dramatic match" - but that is somewhat of an understatement.

The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

But Zheng held firm and reeled off seven games in a row to secure a remarkable 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over the 22nd seed and crowd favourite.

Keys, who won the 2025 Australian Open, appeared to be cruising towards a commanding victory after wrapping up the opening set in just 23 minutes.

But Zheng, who is rebuilding her career after undergoing elbow surgery last year, rallied, clinching it on a tie-break before snatching victory from the jaws of defeat against the American.

Zheng threw herself to the floor in relief and reflected afterwards on a difficult 12 months in which she has questioned if she will rediscover her form.

"Finally, a bit of luck is on my side," the 23-year-old said.

"I am just telling myself ever give up. Somehow, little by little, it's just happened.

"Tennis sometimes feels like rollercoaster. You see many times people have a match point, but at the end we made a comeback."

The Chinese star is the first qualifier to reach the women's fourth round at the US Open since Britain's Emma Raducanu, who went on to win the 2021 title.

'I forgot how to compete' - but Zheng rises again

Three months ago, Zheng could not hold back her tears in a news conference after a first-round exit at the French Open.

It was her first Grand Slam since undergoing surgery in July 2025 to correct a chronic injury caused by small pieces of bone floating in the elbow.

The injury came after a breakthrough 2024 where she reached the Australian Open final, won Olympic gold and made the US Open quarter-finals.

She had also enjoyed a promising start to 2025 before injury struck, advancing to the last eight at Roland Garros and climbing to a career-high of fourth in the world rankings.

It was understandable, therefore, why Zheng found a first-round defeat in Paris this year difficult to take - even if it was to eventual runner-up Maja Chwalinska after nine months on the sidelines.

Her ranking dropped as low as 160 and she had to contest a Grand Slam qualifying event for the first time in four years.

"After coming back from injury I felt I lost the energy and I forgot how to compete," she said.

Zheng seems to have recaptured some of her best form, having been taken to three sets in four of her six matches in New York so far.

She did not meet criteria for a protected ranking - for which players can apply if they are out injured for at least six months - because she made an early comeback to play her home tournament in Beijing in October 2025.

That meant she had to come through qualifying - something she found difficult to accept.

"I was even crying after I won the third match to reach the main draw," Zheng said.

"The main draw is just the beginning where all the players start. That was my beginning before.

"I fight so hard just to start like everyone else. For me, that was really not easy."

Her composure was on display against Keys - especially at 5-4 0-15 down, when she was forced to stop her service motion after a baby started crying in the crowd.

"If it's adult, probably I will look at him very hard or start to speak, but it's just a baby," Zheng joked.

"I can't do anything, you know? It's just a baby."

Zheng went on to win the next four points to level the tie - and the rest was history.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Taylor Fritz and Flavio Cobolli out as six of top 10 men's seeds fall in first week
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz and Flavio Cobolli lose in the third round as six top-10 seeds are knocked out of the men's singles in the first week at the US Open.
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz was unable to explain how he let a two-set lead slip against Francisco Cerundolo as he became one of six top-10 seeds to be eliminated from the men's draw in the first week of the US Open.

The American ninth seed was in complete control and went an early break up in the third set, only for Argentina's Cerundolo to produce a shock 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 win to reach the fourth round.

Less than an hour later, fifth seed Flavio Cobolli of Italy fell to a 7-6 (7-4) 3-6 0-6 3-6 defeat by Belgium's Alexander Blockx, opening up the men's draw even further.

"I don't even know what to say," Fritz said. "I don't really want to talk to anybody, see anybody.

"I need to get out for a couple days and then get back to work. I don't know how I let that happen today."

Cerundolo and 28th seed Blockx will now meet in the fourth round with a place in the quarter-finals up for grabs.

This year's biggest shock at Flushing Meadows was also the first, as Novak Djokovic was beaten by Argentina's Mariano Navone on the opening day's play.

Fourth seed Djokovic was eyeing an historic 25th Grand Slam title but was left in tears after a five-set loss to the world number 49.

Next to go was 10th seed Arthur Fils. The Frenchman was another first-round casualty as he went down in four sets against former world number three Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece.

The highest seed ousted thus far is Canada's Felix Auger-Aliassime, the third seed, who lost to Karen Khachanov in round two, the same stage at which sixth seed Alex de Minaur was beaten.

Those exits looked to have cleared the way for Fritz and Cobolli to go deep into the tournament, but it was an opportunity neither were able to take.

For Fritz, a finalist at Flushing Meadows in 2024, the frustration is all the greater at his home Slam.

He was bidding to become the fifth American through to the fourth round at this year's tournament. With no Jannik Sinner to contend with and Carlos Alcaraz only recently returned from a wrist injury, excitement was growing that, 23 years on from Andy Roddick's US Open triumph, there may finally be another home winner in the men's singles.

That chance persists - but Fritz will know he has let a golden opportunity slip.

Zheng goes from 5-0 and match point down to victory

Gauff wins but mixed fortunes for home hopes at US Open

The chance of a maiden Grand Slam title has also escaped Cobolli for another few months after his capitulation against Blockx.

Having edged the first set on a tie-break, the Italian lost his way and after surrendering the third set to love in just 20 minutes, could not recover.

"I think my energy was a little bit lower than the other days," he said. "I feel a little bit more tight and maybe more tired."

Cobolli admitted Blockx deserved the win and would support him in the next round.

"Alex is very good guy outside the court. He deserved to win, and he won," he added.

Defeats for Cobolli and Fritz mean that apart from top seed Alexander Zverev, only two top-20 players remain in the top half of the draw in 14th seed Learner Tien and 17th seed Jakub Mensik - and they play one another on Friday.

It means Zverev could feasibly reach the final without playing a top-10 player and will not have to face anyone in the top 20 before the semis.

In the men's doubles, British pair Arthur Fery and Joshua Paris progressed with a 6-4 5-7 6-4 win over Anirudh Chandrasekar of India and Ivan Liutarevich of Belarus.

Britain's Neal Skupski and American partner Christian Harrison, the fifth seeds, also advanced as they beat French duo Arthur Reymond and Luca Sanchez 6-0 7-6 (7-3).

But there was disappointment for David Stevenson and Marcus Willis as they lost 5-7 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 to France's 11th seeds Sadio Doumbia and Fabien Reboul.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Coco Gauff wins but Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys out
articles.summary: Coco Gauff reaches the US Open fourth round but last year's finalist Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys go out on a mixed day for home hopes.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff marched into the fourth round of the US Open but compatriots Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys exited on a mixed day for home hopes in New York.

Gauff, the most recent American champion in New York in 2023, did not have things all her own way but maintained her bid for a second triumph by overcoming Spain's Cristina Bucsa 6-3 6-4.

However, Keys said she felt "scared" as she slumped to defeat despite leading her third set against China's Zheng Qinwen 5-0, while last year's runner-up Anisimova lost in straight sets.

But there still will be five American women in the last 16, with teenager Iva Jovic winning later on Saturday to join Gauff, Jessica Pegula, Taylor Townsend and Emma Navarro.

American players could also contest five of the eight fourth-round matches in the men's draw, with Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe, Tommy Paul and Alex Michelsen through - and Learner Tien still to play.

Zheng goes from 5-0 and match point down to victory

Fritz and Cobolli shocked as men's seeds tumble

Gauff 'enjoying the experience' despite expectation

Despite the weight of expectation that she has had to deal with from a young age at her home major, the 22-year-old Gauff is through to the second week at the US Open for a fifth successive year.

Gauff, who became the first American teenager to win the US Open since Serena Williams in 1999 with her breakthrough major success three years ago, heads into the fourth round as the form player in the women's game.

Victory over Bucsa was the 2025 French Open winner's eighth straight-set WTA Tour-level win in a row.

The fourth round is where Gauff's US Open challenge ended in the previous two editions, and she admitted that she struggled to handle the pressure last year.

But in recovering from a 3-1 deficit in the first set, and producing an immediate response to being broken to love in the second, Gauff demonstrated she is better placed to cope with that this time.

"I feel like I'm used to getting to the second week now. I woke up today and I was like 'oh we're already in round three'," Gauff said.

"There's expectations, being American, and I want to do well in front of the fans.

"Last year, I put so much pressure on myself. I'm enjoying the experience out here."

Gauff goes on to face 14th seed Jovic, who came through a pulsating contest against Filipina sensation Alexandra Eala.

Both players showed why they are already firmly in the WTA Tour spotlight during a high-quality battle which ended in Jovic securing a 7-5 3-6 7-5 victory after three hours and three minutes.

Keys appeared on course for a first fourth-round appearance at her home slam since 2023 after taking a commanding third set lead against Olympic champion Zheng.

But the 2025 Australian Open winner would miss a match point and lose each of the final seven games in a 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 loss that stunned the crowd.

The 31-year-old Keys said she felt as though she "couldn't play tennis anymore" in the final set.

"I obviously got off to a really good lead, and then I got really scared, like I couldn't swing [the racquet]," Keys said.

"I felt like I couldn't play tennis anymore. It just felt like it was a much bigger deal than just playing a tennis match all of a sudden."

Keys, who lost the 2017 US Open final to fellow American Sloane Stephens, went out in the fourth round at the other three majors in 2026.

"I feel like I've been struggling for a while now. I'm going to have to make some sort of changes," Keys said.

"I just kind of keep putting it off because that's how the tennis world works. It's just to the point where I actually need to do something about it."

Anisimova, beaten by world number one Aryna Sabalenka in last year's US Open final, lost in straight sets to Russian-born Austrian 24th seed Anastasia Potapova.

The 25-year-old was visibly frustrated with herself throughout the contest, losing her serve twice in the first set and four times in a topsy-turvy second.

Meanwhile, two-time champion Naomi Osaka fought back from a break down in the decider to see off Belgian 23rd seed Elise Mertens.

Osaka, seeded 13th, won 6-3 3-6 7-5 to set up a last-16 match against second seed Elena Rybakina.

Kazakhstan's Rybakina, who knows she will be guaranteed to become the new world number one if she reaches the semi-finals, demonstrated her quality in a 7-6 (8-6) 6-3 victory over Ukraine's Yuliia Starodubtseva.

articles.title: US Open: 18-year-old Iva Jovic ends Alex Eala's run in slugfest between young stars
articles.summary: It took one of the best matches of the tournament to stop Alex Eala at the US Open.
articles.body:
If Saturday's Iva Jovic-Alex Eala match is a sign of things to come, tennis has a bright future. But it will be only Jovic playing over the next few days.

The 18-year-old American ended the Alex Eala show at the US Open with a 7-5, 3-7, 7-5 win over the 21-year-old Filipino star in the third round on Saturday. Her reward will be No. 4 seed Coco Gauff in the fourth round.

The match was between a pair of good friends, but turned into one of the most intense battles of the entire tournament. Both players are great ball-strikers. Neither have serves you would describe as elite or even above-average in a Grand Slam draw. Both chose to stay on the baseline and play the angles.

Tennis is more than just winners and unforced errors but that ratio showed how crisp the contact was, with Jovic posting 44 winners to 27 unforced errors, compared to 34 and 33 for Eala.

Jovic's forehand in particular stood out, especially when directed to the same side toward the left-handed Eala's own forehand. It was a rewarding shot in the first set, and for much of the rest of the match.

The match was break points galore (Jovic 9 of 17, Eala 8 of 20), with the split of points win almost even between servers and returners. The whole thing lasted more than three hours, giving the largely pro-Eala crowd at Arthur Ashe Stadium the spectacle it wanted … and leaving men's No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev to begin his own match with the clock nearing 11 p.m. local time.

It was draining for both participants, and Jovic ended up not minding:

"That felt like a marathon and I felt like I lost my sanity five times over to win that match, but it's really worth it for this feeling. I'm usually not one that shows that many emotions, but this one meant a lot to me."

The same probably can't be said for Eala, who was gracious as she congratulated Jovic and acknowledged the crowd, then left somberly through the tunnel. It's been an incredible season for a young player who carries the hopes of her native Philippines into every match, but she simply ran into an opponent capable of matching her best on Saturday.

The match looked winnable for Eala when she led 4-2 in the third set. Breaks and holds had no meaning in this match, but all she needed was two games at a time when momentum was definitely on her side.

Speaking again on ESPN later, Jovic spoke about the physical toll the match took on her:

"Playing on Arthur Ashe, in front of that atmosphere, I felt like I was shaking throughout the entire match. I lost my earrings midway through. I got them back. There was a time I was literally splat on the floor … I have cuts on my knees. I had to give absolutely everything to get through that."

The win continues Jovic's own breakout season, which she began with a quarterfinal appearance at the Australian Open that was only ended by top seed Aryna Sabalenka. She reached the third round at Roland-Garros, only to run into Naomi Osaka. Her fourth-round opponent at Wimbledon: Jessica Pegula.

Gauff figures to be a similar challenge, but Jovic gave plenty of reason to expect an upset with her form Saturday. Per ESPN , she's the youngest American woman to reach three Grand Slam fourth rounds in a single year since Venus Williams in 1998.

"I didn't play amazing ​and it was getting me down, sorry about my ​behaviour, for the little kids watching," said Osaka, who threw her racket ​to the floor at one point.

"This is my favourite tournament. I wanted ⁠to play well in front of you. I'm just that glad I have the opportunity to play another match.

"I thought I was going to be ok, but clearly I was ⁠shaky."

Jovic puts friendship with Eala on hold to win three-hour battle

Home hope Iva Jovic and ‌Alexandra Eala of the Philippines put their friendship aside for three hours before the 18-year-old American prevailed 7-5 3-6 7-5 on Arthur ​Ashe Stadium to reach the fourth round.

The two rising stars and close friends had already shared the ​court in New York during Fan Week when ‌they teamed up with their fathers for a light-hearted doubles hit.

Jovic edged a tight opening set but Eala responded in the second as the 21-year-old ​raising her level to force a decider.

The final ⁠set again featured momentum swings, with ⁠Jovic trailing 4-2 before fighting back to close out the victory and extend her head-to-head record ‌against Eala to 3-0, with a win on each of the three surfaces.

"That felt like a marathon. I felt like I lost ‌my sanity five times over to win that match. But it's really worth it for this feeling," Jovic said on court.

"I'm usually not one that shows that many emotions. But this one really meant a ⁠lot to me. It's everything to have another ​match at the US Open."

articles.title: Jovic moved to tears after beating ‘incredible’ friend Eala in US Open epic
articles.summary: Iva Jovic outlasted the fellow young tennis sensation from the Philippines, Alex Eala, in an epic three-hour showdown.
articles.body:
American teen Iva Jovic was moved to tears while talking about her off-court friend and on-court opponent Alex Eala, whom she beat in a three-set thriller to enter the round of 16 at the US Open.

Jovic outlasted the fellow young tennis sensation from the Philippines in an epic three-hour showdown on Saturday to book a meeting with fourth-seeded former champion Coco Gauff.

The 14th-seed Jovic won five of the last six games for a 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 triumph over 17th-seed Eala after three hours and three minutes.

“That felt like a marathon, and I felt like I lost my sanity five times over to win that match,” Jovic said. “But it’s really worth it for this feeling.”

Two of the top rising stars of women’s tennis made their Arthur Ashe Stadium debut a memorable battle that featured 17 service breaks in 33 games.

“That match, definitely the way it finished, deserved that court,” Jovic said.

“It literally took everything to somehow squeeze my way through that.”

When the emerging US tennis star’s win was sealed, her Filipina friend went around the court to congratulate her instead of waiting at the net as players usually do at the end of tennis matches.

When Jovic was asked about Eala’s gesture in her post-match news conference, the American was moved to tears and said it showed her friend’s character.

“It says a lot about her as a person,” Jovic said while wiping away tears. “I’m gonna start crying, but it says a lot about her as a person to be able to do that after that type of match and still come over to hug me and wish me all the best. And even in the locker room behind closed doors … so that just says a lot about her and her character. Yeah, she’s incredible.”

Jovic, 18, and Eala, 21, are friends and sometimes doubles partners, knowing each other’s skills and style well. That helped produce seven service breaks in the first 11 games.

“I’m usually not one that shows that many emotions, but this one really meant a lot to me. It’s everything to have another match here at the US Open,” Jovic said.

That match will be against compatriot Gauff, the 2023 US Open and 2025 French Open champion.

“I’m going to be more than happy to just bring this fight and this energy, and whatever happens I can leave with my head high,” Jovic said.

Jovic broke four times to win the first set but was broken three times by left-hander Eala to drop the second.

“The level was absolutely incredible from both sides,” Jovic said.

“We definitely put on a show, and it literally took everything to get through that … losing my earrings, falling literally flat-out on the floor, cuts on my knees, mental breakdowns,” she said.

Eala admitted: “I had my chances. I’m happy with the match in general. Of course there is disappointment in losing, but trying to see the positive side. It was a really good match. The level was really high.

“I left everything out there. I fought through the ups and downs … What I know for a fact is that I fought, so I’m happy with that.”

A quarterfinalist at this year’s Australian Open, Jovic won her first WTA title last year in Guadalajara at age 17.

She beat Eala at the French Open and Queen’s Club in London earlier this season in their prior meetings, but that was before Eala won her first WTA title at Washington.

“She played an outrageous level tonight. She was serving very good. She was showing a lot more versatility with her returns,” Jovic said of Eala.

“She’s playing some of the best tennis in the world right now, so it’s no doubt it takes a hell of an effort to beat her.”

articles.title: US Open: No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka moves on to quarterfinals with straight-sets victory over Taylor Townsend
articles.summary: Townsend had the crowd on her side at Arthur Ashe Stadium, but was ultimately no match for the top-ranked women's player.
articles.body:
Aryna Sabalenka avoided the stumbles that top seeds encountered during Saturday's third-round action at the US Open by dispatching Taylor Townsend to move on to the quarterfinals.

The women's No. 1 seed faced a battle from the unseeded American, but eventually won in straight sets, 6-4, 6-3, on Sunday and will face the winner between No. 6 Linda Nosková and No. 11 Marta Kostyuk next as she pursues her third consecutive US Open championship.

Sabalenka has won 17 consecutive matches in Flushing and has advanced to the quarterfinals for the sixth straight year.

Townsend, who advanced to the fourth round by getting past No. 15 Diana Shnaider on Friday, wasn't overwhelmed by Sabalenka's serve as many of her opponents often are, and broke twice early in the first set. But she hurt herself by hitting several returns wide or long.

When Townsend tied the first set at 2-2, Sabalenka appeared as if frustration might unsettle her as it has when she's struggled previously. Instead, she channeled whatever anger she may have been feeling into several strong returns. After breaking Townsend's serves, Sabalenka held to go ahead 4-2 and settled in.

Townsend had the support of the crowd of her fellow Americans at Arthur Ashe Stadium — which Sabalenka couldn't resist alluding to during her post-match interview — but made too many unforced errors and allowed Sabalenka to lock in.

Sabalenka appeared to have momentum as the second set began, but Townsend was able to hold serve. Throughout the match, she caught Sabalenka off guard with her play at the net, charging shots that were seemingly out of reach.

Townsend went ahead in the second set, catching Sabalenka flat-footed with consecutive aces and eventually broke her serve to take a 3-1 lead. That roused the crowd to get louder for Townsend, but Sabalenka regained control by breaking back and then holding serve.

After Sabalenka tied the set at 3-3, Townsend began to falter by misfiring on a forehand return and then double-faulting. Sabalenka broke serve twice to win three consecutive games. Perhaps sensing a win in hand, she found the accuracy on her returns, nailing a cross-court backhand. The American underdog couldn't recover from there.

Despite losing in straight sets, Townsend did provide some tough opposition and capitalized on Sabalenka not controlling her serve — especially early in that second set. As the defending champion moves on to the quarterfinals, Sabalenka may encounter more difficulties against players who can take advantage when she doesn't hold serve. Not beating themselves with mistakes could also help.

articles.title: US Open 2026: Defending champions Carlos Alcaraz and Aryna Sabalenka reach quarter-finals
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz puts on exhibition as a straight-sets victory over Tommy Paul seals passage to US Open quarter-finals; women's world No 1 Aryna Sabalenka also into last eight after edging past Taylor Townsend; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
The Spaniard, still showing no signs of the wrist injury that sidelined him for more than four months before the tournament, dismantled American Tommy Paul in straight sets.

Alcaraz is already the youngest man to complete a career Grand Slam and should he go on to win back-to-back Flushing Meadows crowns, he would become the only man in the Open Era to successfully defend major titles on all three surfaces.

Having won on the grass of Wimbledon in 2023 and 2024 and on the French Open clay in 2024 and last year, the 23-year-old can complete the set on hard courts if he triumphs next Sunday.

Paul, the 20th seed, had talked up his chances before the match, saying "I like to think of myself as somebody who always thinks I can beat those (top) players".

But a 6-4 6-3 6-4 defeat means Alcaraz has now beaten the 29-year-old six times in a row, winning the last 14 sets they have contested.

He actually faced two set points at the end of the third, but swatted them away with two contemptuous forehand winners on his way to victory in two hours and 21 minutes.

'I think I'm back to full power' - Alcaraz issues US Open warning

"I played my game. I tried to put my style on today's match.

"Tommy is such a talented player and his shots are dangerous and hard to control, so I just tried to be ready for the battle, ready to run if it mattered.

"I tried to be aggressive all the time and tried not to let him stay on the court. I put so much pressure on the return game. It helped a lot to play relaxed, calm and to think clearly.

"I'm really happy with the performance today. Am I back to full power? I think so. I play well every time I come here, and I just try to enjoy it.

"It doesn't matter I was out for four-and-a-half months; every time I come here I play my best."

Alcaraz 'different class' and 'in another stratosphere'

"It's a pleasure to watch Alcaraz go through the gears. He's just got better and better as this tournament has gone on.

"Tommy Paul gave it everything he had but, at the end of the day, Alcaraz was different class.

"The forehand was firing. I've seen plenty of good forehands over the years, but I think Alcaraz's might be the best. It's unbelievable how he hits it so hard and doesn't look like missing."

Sky Sports Tennis' Martina Navratilova :

"It's really crazy he got this good this fast. Normally, when people have that many options to their game, it takes a while to figure out how to play the game. But not Carlos, he's just in another stratosphere."

Sabalenka edges Townsend to reach last eight

Aryna Sabalenka clung onto her US Open title and the world No 1 spot after an unconvincing win over Taylor Townsend.

The Belarusian battled through 6-4 6-3 on Arthur Ashe Stadium in a bizarre match which featured 11 breaks of serve from 19 games.

Sabalenka has spent 99 weeks at the top of the rankings but she needs to win a third straight Flushing Meadows title - and for current No 2 Elena Rybakina to lose before the semi-finals - if she is to reach a century.

"It's super challenging but once again it's important to focus on yourself," said Sabalenka, who had to come from a breakdown in the second set against popular American Townsend.

"I was like 'okay, you are down the break, just try to return the serve and put as much pressure on her as possible'.

"I was just trying to stay focused on myself, not only point by point but ball by ball. I'm happy I was able to turn around the second set, I think it was a key moment."

In the quarter-finals Sabalenka will play Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova, after the Czech came through a titanic battle against Marta Kostyuk in a repeat of their semi-final at SW19.

Ukrainian Kostyuk saved five match points, two at the end of the second set and three in the decider, before Noskova eventually got over the line 7-5 5-7 6-4.

"It was good enough. It was pretty solid. Townsend had more winners but Aryna did really well returning serve and with passing shots.

"Townsend tried to come into the net more, but she wasn't successful there, that's how well Sabalenka played from the baseline.

"Overall, I would give Sabalenka a 'B' because she lost her serve so many times, but she played really well when it mattered."

"There was a lot of ferocious intensity to what Sabalenka brought onto this court. When she went a break down in the second set, she really galvanised herself. When she got back on track, she let out the most enormous shriek and you just knew she meant business.

"The passion, the aura, the mentality, the personality, she brings so much to every court. She's a great showwoman and puts on a show whenever she plays tennis. She understands this isn't just sport, it's entertainment as well.

"She is going to take some beating. She doesn't look as vulnerable as I was expecting. So far, she hasn't dropped a set and looks in very good shape."

articles.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulates Serena Williams by overcoming Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final.
articles.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulated Serena Williams as she eventually overpowered American Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final.

A topsy-turvy contest featured 10 breaks of serve, but Sabalenka recovered from 3-1 down in the second serve to seal a 6-4 6-3 victory with a fifth consecutive game.

It was the Belarusian's 18th consecutive win at the tournament, extending her three-year unbeaten streak following back-to-back triumphs in 2024 and 2025.

Sabalenka, 28, is the first woman to reach six consecutive singles quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows since American great Williams in 2016.

Six-time champion Williams was also the last player to win three US Open titles in a row, and Sabalenka is now three wins from matching that feat.

She will face Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova for a semi-final place, after the Czech sixth seed required six match points to overcome Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk in a rollercoaster 7-5 5-7 6-4 win.

Despite the straightforward scoreline this was a tricky match which required a resilient display from Sabalenka, who also had the vast majority of the crowd against her.

In that context this was an impressive victory for the four-time major winner, who has not always managed to maintain her composure in similarly testing scenarios.

"I was just trying to stay focused on myself, not only point by point but ball by ball," Sabalenka said.

"I'm happy I was able to turn around the second set, I think it was a key moment."

Alcaraz delivers statement win to reach last eight

No Brits left in US Open singles - but are there reasons to be positive?

Williams sisters exit US Open but excite - what does future hold?

The match began with five successive breaks of serve - mostly due to excellent returning by both players - but it was Sabalenka who finally took charge.

Doubles specialist Townsend, who walked out wearing a long, black-feathered outfit, continued to frustrate Sabalenka and forced her to serve out the set at the second opportunity, before making the breakthrough in the second set.

But Sabalenka, aware she must lift the trophy to have a chance of retaining her number one ranking, produced an immediate reply as she broke back to love.

That signalled the start of Sabalenka's dash to the finish line. The top seed lost just five points across the final five games to end Townsend's challenge in 75 minutes.

Sabalenka was full of praise for Townsend, saying: "What an incredible player she is, approaching the net, a great returner, moving well, very brave.

"You can see how focused she was. It was really challenging playing her, especially here.

"Thank you so much [to the crowd] for being so respectful to me. I knew coming into this match that you guys would be on her side, but you were sometimes cheering for me and I really appreciate that."

At home on the US Open hard courts, Sabalenka has not failed to reach the semi-finals here since 2020.

But, following a fourth-round exit at Wimbledon, she is aiming to avoid a first season without a major title since 2022.

Noskova's sense of relief was cleared as she crouched to the ground after taking her sixth match point about an hour after earning her first.

The 21-year-old served for the match in the second set, but missed her first two match points as Kostyuk battled back from 5-3 down to force a decider.

The players exchanged breaks of serve in a tense final set, but it was Noskova who emerged, once again, with a 5-3 advantage.

Noskova failed to take her next two match points as a couple of misses helped Kostyuk to deuce, and missed her fifth after saving a break point, before finally getting over the line after an emotionally draining two and a half hours on court.

"I am more than relieved, this match was so tough, emotionally a bit more than physically," Noskova said.

"Today was very close, it could have ended both ways. With all the chances I had in the second set, it was tough to still kind of restart."

articles.summary: No permitió que un buen Tommy Paul llegara a inquietarle
articles.body: La verdad es que hay que esforzarse en recordar que Carlos Alcaraz ha pasado casi medio año sin jugar por lesión. Y que, sin periodo de adaptación ni rodaje reaparece en este US Open, un Grand Slam y por tanto al mejor de cinco sets, con rivales de gran calidad desde muy pronto. Porque en Flushing Meadows estamos viendo al Carlos Alcaraz de siempre, el jugador versátil y efectivo que ha convertido la victoria en lo normal. Como si no le hubiera pasado nada. Prueba de ello fue su encuentro ante Tommy Paul, ganado por 6-4, 6-3 6-4. Paul es el 21 ATP pero no hace tanto ha sido 'top 10'. Ha ganado dos veces al de El Palmar (aunque la última fuera en 2023, y el español le haya superado en otras seis ocasiones, y ahora en siete) y este año ha sido ya campeón -en Houston-. Pero en este partido no ha tenido ninguna oportunidad ante Carlos, y eso que no ha jugado mal. Lo que le ha sucedido es que se ha encontrado, si no a la mejor versión de Carlos Alcaraz, sí a una muy profesional, sólida en juego y en mentalidad, que tras el 4-4 del primer set ganó cuatro juegos seguidos para ponerse 6-4 y 2-0, y que cuando en el juego siguiente Paul recuperó el 'break', le devolvió el golpe de inmediato. También superó el peligrosísimo momento en que, cuando sacaba ganar, Paul se puso con 15-40. Carlos consiguió, sobre todo, encontrar la solución correcta a cada circunstancia del partido. Estuvo eficaz en la red cuando lo necesitó, dominó de derecha cuando fue necesario y obligó a jugar al límite a su rival con el resultado de obligarle a cometer errores mientras él podía elegir mejor sus tiros. Al final, dos horas y doce minutos para alcanzar los cuartos. En ellos se enfrentará al vencedor del Shelton-Tsitsipas, que se jugará en la noche neoyorquina. Un partido que tendrá historia: siempre ha habido en semifinales de un torneo masculino de Grand Slam un tenista que jugaba revés a una mano. En este torneo sólo Tsitsipas puede mantener la tradición. Para ello, claro, tendrá que vencer a Shelton... y luego a Carlos. Sabalenka sigue buscando el triplete Aryna Sabalenka no había ganado ninguno de sus últimos siete torneos y llegaba a Nueva York rodeada de dudas sobre sus posibilidades de ser tricampeona. Pero ya está en cuartos sin ceder un set (6-4 y 6-3 a Taylor Townsend en octavos) y lleva 17 victorias consecutivas en Flushing Meadows, tras sus triunfos en 2025 y 2025. Elena Rybakina será número 1 si llega a semifinales (sin importar lo que hagan las demás), Jessica Pegula y Coco Gauff, pero Aryna no quiere ‘ayudar’ a sus rivales. En otros encuentros, Noskova venció a Kostyuk 7-5, 5-7, 6-4. En dobles, Cristina Bucsa y Nicole Melichar alcanzaron los octavos de final venciendo a las británicas Dart y Lumsdel 6-2, 6-2

articles.body:
On Sunday, defending US Open champion Carlos Alcaraz cruised past Tommy Paul in what was expected to be his toughest test yet.

In the women's draw, two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka defeated Taylor Townsend in straight sets.

Everything you need, from top takeaways to tomorrow's schedule, is below.

No. 2 Carlos Alcaraz def. No. 20 Tommy Paul, 6-4, 6-3, 6-4

Alex Michelsen def. No. 27 Tomas Martin Etcheverry, 7-6 (6), 6-4, 6-4

Carlos Alcaraz eased any concern about rust, defeating Tommy Paul in straight sets.

The defending champion's forehand looked as strong as ever, while he was able to take advantage of Paul's serving struggles.

Paul had his opportunities to break late in the match, but Alcaraz's forehand was just too effective.

It was the Spaniard's best match since returning from his wrist injury.

Meanwhile, in other action, Alex Michelsen continued his improbable run with another straight-sets win.

The 22-year-old is the first unseeded man this century to reach the US Open quarterfinals without dropping a set.

Against No. 27 Tomas Martin Etcheverry, Michelsen's serve once again stood out.

He won 81 percent of points on his first serve and hit 44 winners.

Michelsen has won at least 75 percent of his first-serve points in all four matches, troubling every opponent with his heavy forehand.

The Round of 16 continues Monday on ESPN, with all matches also being available on ESPN Unlimited.

Francisco Cerundolo (24) vs. Alexander Blockx (28)

Alexander Zverev (1) vs. Luciano Darderi (21)

Match of the Day: Learner Tien (14) vs. Karen Khachanov

On Monday, Learner Tien will look to become the youngest American US Open quarterfinalist since Andy Roddick in 2002.

The 20-year-old enters on the heels of a thrilling five-set win over Jakub Mensik.

His next opponent, Khachanov, is expected to be just as challenging.

Khachanov has been in top form the entire tournament.

The former top-10 player has already earned a signature win this tournament, defeating No. 3 Felix Auger-Aliassime in the second round.

With his grit and the crowd behind him, Tien is certainly capable of winning this match.

However, with his experience and dangerous forehand, Khachanov should be able to persevere.

Prediction: Karen Khachanov def. No. 14 Learner Tien in 4 sets

No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka def. Taylor Townsend, 6-4, 6-3

No. 6 Linda Noskova def. No. 11 Marta Kostyuk, 7-5, 5-7, 6-4

Aryna Sabalenka continued her quest for a third straight US Open title with a straight-sets win over Taylor Townsend.

The four-time champion played her signature return game, winning 57 percent of return points.

Despite being broken four times, Sabalenka's baseline consistency and constant redirection proved too much for Townsend.

Townsend found an opening in the second set, going up 3-1; however, Sabalenka was determined to finish in straight sets, rattling off five straight games to win the match.

Mirra Andreeva (5) vs. Anastasia Potapova (24)

Match of the Day: Coco Gauff (4) vs. Iva Jovic (14)

Arthur Ashe Stadium spectators will catch an All-American thriller between Coco Gauff and Iva Jovic Monday night.

Gauff enters the Round of 16 on the heels of another convincing win.

The two-time major champion is in arguably the best form of her career, having won nine straight matches without dropping a set.

Gauff has found her consistent tennis while continuing to suffocate her opponents with her return game.

Meanwhile, Jovic enters on the heels of winning arguably the most thrilling match of the tournament.

The 18-year-old defeated Alexandra Eala in a three-set match that required three hours to see a victor.

Jovic is in the middle of a breakout season, reaching the Australian Open quarterfinal and the Wimbledon Round of 16.

Jovic has the consistency and fitness to make this a really competitive match.

However, Gauff's aggression and physicality from the baseline are unlike anything Jovic has seen in this tournament, making the prospects of an upset of this magnitude extremely unlikely.

Prediction: No. 4 Coco Gauff def. No. 14 Iva Jovic in 2 sets

articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz continued his march toward his second straight US Open title and third overall with a dominant victory over Tommy Paul in the Round of 16 on Sunday.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz continued his march toward his second straight US Open title and third overall with a dominant victory over Tommy Paul in the Round of 16 on Sunday.

Alcaraz won in straight sets by scores of 6-4, 6-3, 6-4. He's now in the US Open quarterfinals for the fifth time in his career.

The 23-year-old is looking to become the first male competitor to defend his US Open title since Roger Federer won five straight from 2004 to 2008. His 28th career win at the US Open breaks a tie with Pete Sampras for the third-most by any man in his first six appearances in the Open era, putting him behind only John McEnroe (33) and Lleyton Hewitt (29).

Paul, the No. 20 seed, was looking to make it to the quarterfinals of the US Open for the first time in his career. He has now lost 14 consecutive sets to Alcaraz.

It was clear early on that Paul was bringing his best against the defending champ, as neither player earned a break point opportunity through the first nine points of the match. Alcaraz finally took over and broke Paul's serve to end the first set in emphatic fashion.

Alcaraz appeared to be cruising when he jumped out to a 2-0 lead in the second set with another break point. However, Paul earned a break of his own to make things interesting. Undeterred, Alcaraz broke him right back for a third straight time to maintain the advantage.

Still, Paul kept fighting. After falling behind 4-1, he staved off a whopping six break-point chances from Alcaraz to cut into the deficit on a marathon point. Both players held serve back and forth as Alcaraz took the set.

Alcaraz put the pressure on early to start the third set. Paul staved off three break chances before eventually relenting and falling behind 2-1. Both players held serve until Paul started gaining momentum with the match on the line at 5-4. He surprised Alcaraz with two break opportunities, but the Spaniard later battled back to seal the victory.

Alcaraz will face the winner of Sunday's Round of 16 match between No. 8 Ben Shelton and Stefanos Tsitsipas in the quarterfinals on Tuesday.

articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz continues his return from long-term injury with a hugely impressive fourth-round win against Tommy Paul at the US Open.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz continued his return from long-term injury with a hugely impressive fourth-round win against Tommy Paul at the US Open.

Playing just his fourth competitive singles match after an absence of more than four months, the 23-year-old Spaniard produced a masterful performance to beat American 20th seed Paul 6-4 6-3 6-4.

He has dropped only one set on his way to the last eight in New York and his quarter-final opponent will be either American eighth seed Ben Shelton or Greece's Stefanos Tsitsipas.

A wrist injury caused Alcaraz to miss both the French Open and Wimbledon earlier this summer.

He had won the previous two Grand Slams - last year's US Open and this year's Australian Open - meaning the straight-set victory over Paul extended his run of match wins at the majors to 18.

Asked on court if he is back to "full power", Alcaraz smiled as he replied: "I think so. Except for one year since [his US Open debut in] 2021, I've made the quarter-finals here. That shows how special this place is to me and shows how well I'm playing every time I come here.

"I just try to enjoy my time on the court and it doesn't matter that I was out for four and a half months - every time I come here, I play my best."

Shelton and Tsitsipas meet in Sunday's night session and seven-time major champion Alcaraz has never previously lost to either player at Tour level, beating Shelton three times and Tsitsipas on six occasions.

"If Shelton were to come through, he is the kind of player that can knock the racquet out of your hand," said American former player Jeff Tarango on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra.

"It's going to be a real test to see how Alcaraz's wrist is with a 149mph serve coming to that forehand, but Alcaraz should get through Shelton if his wrist is fine."

Sabalenka overcomes tricky Townsend test at US Open

How to follow US Open on the BBC Published 4 minutes ago

Alcaraz said after his third-round win that he was happy with the level of fitness he had shown in the early rounds following his lengthy absence, while he demonstrated against Paul that the quality of his shot-making is as good as ever.

One sensational cross-court forehand winner early in the second set, which landed in from an almost impossible angle, was measured at 103mph.

That came shortly after Alcaraz had broken Paul's serve in the 10th game of a tight, high-quality opening set to take it 6-4.

Paul, who was attempting to reach the quarter-finals of his home Grand Slam for the first time, battled hard throughout but Alcaraz proved to be too strong.

Paul had two break points when Alcaraz served for the match at 5-4 in the third set, but the two-time US Open champion put together a run of four straight points to seal victory.

Former British number one Tim Henman told Sky Sports: "When you haven't played tennis for four weeks, it seems a lot and you can be a bit rusty. This is four and a half months.

"If you would have given Alcaraz a blank piece of paper at the beginning of the tournament and asked how he'd want the first four matches to go, he would have scripted it exactly like that.

"He's had a few slightly challenging moments but, in the important moments, he's just come up with incredible tennis. That's got to give him so much confidence moving forward."
